A keen mind and skillful tongue you possess. Your points are not without merit, and wisdom dictates we concede.
Sometimes the second hammer-stroke may reveal gems yet unseen. We accept.
A bargain well struck.
By my beard, that's a fairer offer. You convinced me.
This second offer is indeed better than your first. You have proven a shrewd negotiator.
A reasonable counter. We accept, such as it is.
Do not be troubled, for we agree to your new terms. The arrangements will be made.
Indeed, your words hold the weight of foresight. I see the path now, though it be shrouded in mist.
Very well. Your wisdom echoes in my heart, and I am moved to agree.
Carathon i iest lîn. Perhaps your wisdom sees to depths I have overlooked before.
A minor compromise for the greater end. It seems that wisdom has found root in unlikely soil. I will accept.
We proceed, for though the terms perhaps are a crooked path askew from my intent, such a path yet leads forward.
This concession to my designs is thus imperfect, yet tolerable. So be it.
Your terms hold merit, though not as first hoped. We find them acceptable.
You speak in riddles sometimes. Will you stop if I accept?
Agreed. It is not the path we sought, yet it leads to steadier ground.
A wise speaker. There is real worth behind thy words, and for that I give commendation.
It would suit thee better to lie more. I would notice it, but it would get thee further in the Black Land. No matter, I accept.
If it must be so, then I will accept. Do not expect thy haggling to work every time.
Hmph. You’ve offered better than before... enough that I won’t gut you.
You finally talk sense. This is a wiser offer. We'll accept, for now.
Your offer isn't as worthless as before. I agree. But my warcamp sees no delight in it.
Then let it be so. Your terms are hard, but just. The honour of the Mark demands we accept this pact.
Aye, we accept your counter. May fortune favour us all in the days to come, for woe betide those who break faith.
So be it. We will meet these new conditions. Let the horn blow to signal our assent; the bargain is sealed.
A proposal rich in wisdom. We accept.
Oh? Many at the bazaar could learn from you. We have an agreement.
Your wisdom carries with the wind. Though the breeze changes, it carries us to the path of prosperity.
Good enough. Not what was asked. Not what was feared.
Your second words strike better than your first. Done.
New words atop old ones. But better. We accept.

diplomacy_strings_string_counter_reject_.value_original: You must think the heirs of Elendil destitute indeed if you seek such a brazen bargain. We cannot accept.
Your proposed alterations render the agreement untenable for us. It seems our paths must diverge on this matter.
Your counter-offer is unacceptable. Our terms were clear and just; we shall not be haggled with like peddlers on an outlying market.
Yer tryin' to haggle me down to bedrock, are ye? I've seen more generosity from a cave-troll!
Hmph! This offer of yours is barely worth the parchment it's written on. I'd sooner trust a goblin with my ale cellar.
That's yer offer? You insult me with such a pittance! Forget it, lad.
Why would we accept a lesser offer? Your haggling is not proving beneficial.
To accept this would bring great dishonour. I suggest you rethink your proposal again.
No. We are not so desparate that we'd accept such a one-sided arrangement. Balance the scales and we may be interested.
The river of accord, once clear, now muddies with your insistence. Regrettably, we cannot accept such a devaluation of shared purpose.
The light fades from my welcome. Such a bargain leaves us poorer than before, and leaves me little faith in the harvest to come.
Your words echo hollowly in these ancient halls. Seek counsel amongst your own; perhaps wiser voices might prevail.
Such terms may suffice elsewhere. Isengard requires more.
The tower does not bend to compromise. Nor to weakness.
I had hoped for clarity. Instead, you offer confusion. Your terms are thus declined.
This proposal is worse than the last. You betray yourself and reveal your desparation.
We have reviewed your amended terms, and they fall short of what honour and necessity demand.
Even tempered anew, your offer fails to bridge the divide. I must decline.
Not even the most desparate snaga would accept that. Insult me further, and this meeting will be over.
I speak for the immortal ruler of this Earth, Sauron the Great, not some runt king. Remember that next time.
Oh? Did I mishear thee? I thought I was speaking with a diplomat, not some simple-minded child.
You bargain like a fool. This deal is dead, as will you be if you linger.
Twist my words again and I'll twist your head 'round til it's on backwards.
You call this a counteroffer? Here, take this shrakh-bucket. That's what it's worth.
That is a fool's bargain, fit only for those who value silver above their souls. Seek elsewhere for weakness, for you will not find it here.
We hear your words, but they ring hollow. This is no true offer, and we reject it outright.
Enough! We grow weary of this dance. We will take what is ours by right, not by your grudging hand.
You are now lost in your attempts to chart these negotiations.
We travel far and this is the reception? You bore us.
Bicker amongst yourselves. We have journeys to plan.
I grow tired of words. Go, or let us decide with a brawl.
Enough with this banter. I am going back into the open air, to see what the wind and sky are doing!
You talk like a weakling. I do not speak with weaklings.

diplomacy_strings_string_demand_break_de.value_original: The eyes of the White Tower see much. You are in league with those that would seek to further the Dark Lord's influence. Forsake this bond, for the good of all Free People!
The Dúnedain, who see further than most, bid you cut this thread to false allies before it strangles you at unawares.
The Enemy is ever weaving his web of deceit. For your own sake, and for the hope of the West, sever ties that bind you to ill counsel.
Think ye can sup with devils and dine with dwarves? Nay, lad! Choose yer friends wisely, and ditch those treacherous dogs before we decide for ye.
I'm sayin' it plain! That so-called alliance o' yers is an insult to every dwarf-forged blade ever hammered.
This ain't a request, it's a bloody demand! You're consortin' with goblin-scum and expect to be treated with respect? Get wise, and ditch 'em now.
My Chieftain conquers what he sees. Stand with the doomed, and be doomed also.
Our clans need more land, and we have found some. You must not stand with them, or you will surely perish.
You have hitched your cart to a dying horse. That kingdom will fall, and you with it, should you not sever your bond.
The currents of fate carry you towards a ruinous shore. Abandon this alliance, lest you be dashed upon the rocks of their inevitable demise.
The trees themselves weep at your ill-chosen fellowship. Gin iallon, I beseech you to renounce it, and let the light of reason guide your path once more
Your alliance with the enemy casts a long shadow, marring much of what is fair. Sever it now, or find yourself adrift in a darkness of your own making.
A new power is rising. Against it, the old allies and policies will not avail us at all. It would be wise to abandon them, my friend.
You cling to bonds forged in weakness. Break them, lest you be dragged down with them.
Your strength is not your own while their weight drags at your feet. Cast it off.
It seems less evil to counsel another man to break truth than to do so oneself.
Your alliance binds you to a cause we cannot abide. If peace with us is your aim, then you must sever your treaty.
Not all ties are worth the cost they carry. Sever yours before it drags you into shadow not your own.
Even I can see the dealings thou maketh in the dark, where the Master might not see. Know that He does, and He would have them cease, lest His attention focus on thee further.
I am told of thy kingdoms treatises, and how thou treat with the enemy. Break all contact and be grateful of thy existence.
An enemy of Lugbúrz has made a dirty nest beside thy throne. Rid them from thy side, lest we intervene.
Break your alliance. Now. Or we break you. No warnings, no second chances.
If you stand with them, you stand against the Orcs. End your treaty, or we'll end you.
You raise your shield for them? I tell you to drop it, or we drop your corpses in the dark.
The winds of fate have shifted, and the enemy you embrace seeks to destroy all that we hold dear. Renounce them, and let us ride together against the coming storm.
The oath you swore is forfeit; the company you keep is poisoned. Let honour guide you now. Choose, and choose wisely.
Hear me, for this is my final word: sunder your bond. Ere the sun rises again, let your banners fly free of their stain, or know our wrath.
You would defend the enemies of Harad? End this before the oasis shrivels.
Show your wisdom! Stand against those condemned by the sands.
So you would ally yourselves with the dark side of the dunes? We will not tolerate deals behind our backs.
You are in bed with those who set fire to our fields. Set fire to your alliance!
Their shield is poison. Cast it down.
You mingle with wolves, their howl becomes yours. Break with them or hear ours rise louder!

diplomacy_strings_string_demand_join_war.value_original: The defence of all Free Peoples rests upon our shoulders. Will you not join your strength to ours, that this encroaching darkness might be thrown back from our borders?
Orodruin spews forth clouds of darkness, as the dawnless days draw nigh. The beacons are lit, and we call to aid any that would still oppose the Enemy.
Here will the hammer-stroke fall hardest, and if we fall, who shall stand? With hope for aid we now look to your steadfast people.
Our scouts bring dire tidings of the Enemy's muster. We entreat you, by the bonds of old friendship and shared peril, to stand with us against this common foe ere it is too late.
Your fingers would remember their old strength better, if they grasped a sword-hilt. Let this be the hour when we draw swords together!
Hail, friend of the Dúnedain! I present you the Red Arrow, a token of war. The Lord of Gondor asks for all your strength and your speed, lest we should fall at last.
In this dire hour, the Men of the West call upon you. Will you march with us against the tide of darkness, or shall history mark you as one who stood aside?
The hour is dire, and we do not beg. March with us against the Shadow, or be counted among our foes.
Let this be our final word on the matter. Your swords are needed against the common Enemy. Offer them now, freely, or we shall assume your intent is hostile.
What say ye? Will ye stand shoulder to shoulder with dwarves, or turn a blind eye as they ravage our homes?
Your warriors are renowned, and our axes are sharp. Side with us, and end this threat for good.
Join us. We'll make those beard-waggling troublemakers regret the day they crossed us.
Listen, lad, they'll be coming for you next, mark my words. Join us now, while we still have a chance!
This time we ask you to raise a sword, not a mug of ale. Though we can drink to our victory!
Look, friend, I wouldn't ask if it weren't dire. Our foe grows strong, and we alone cannot hold them back.
Listen here, I need ye to bleed them for us! They've wronged my kin, and a debt must be paid in iron and fire.
Will you stand idle while they mock our ancestors? Fight alongside us, damn you!
Are you deaf? The time for talk is done! Draw your sword and bring ruin upon those craven dogs!
We are aware of your valour and force of arms. Fight with our warriors in this conflict.
The wise adapt; fools resist. Do not be foolish. They cannot fight a war on many fronts.
Our clans march ever forward. Stand with them and fight. Or cower in fear and shame.
Don armour! Bare fangs! Draw blades with us! There will be glory overflowing and riches for all!
Honour calls and we must answer. There is great opportunity for you here. Or would you rather your blades grow rusted?
The Golden Court speaks highly of your men. It is a token of honour that we request you to fight by our side.
Abandon your senseless defiance and march to war with us, lest you be reduced to ash as golden fire covers all.
The will of our Chieftains shall not be broken my nameless fear in a far off land. Nor shall yours if your forces stand with us.
Do you not see that you have been manipulated to serve their ends? Our golden hordes yet shine against the darkness. Have you the strength to defy them?
A festering wound upon the earth spreads its sickness outwards, and if it is not cut out, all shall succumb. The time for cautious peace is past: draw now your blade!
The stars themselves seem dimmer, burdened by the shadow that creeps across the land; join us in defiance, and let our combined might rekindle their ancient fire.
Fân fanna Anor. This black cloud casts shade upon us all, and even now encroaches upon your borders. Stand beside us, and together we shall hew a way back to the light.
It is not our part here to take thought only for a season, or for a few lives of Men, or for a passing age of the world. We should seek a final end of this menace, even if we do not hope to make one.
The trees of my realm weep at the encroaching blight, their leaves turning to ash before their time. Savo chûr an dagor! Cleanse this stain, before it poisons the very heart of Arda.
Iston i vellas lîn ne ndagor. The wind carries wispers of your strength to our forest, and we would have you by our side.
Dago i chyth! You will commit to this fight, and spill blood against the enemy, or be branded forever as allies of the Shadow.
Your people are not safe. Send forth your armies, for only war will cleanse the encroaching stain. What say you: go-vaethathanc ned auth?

Will you stand idly by while this malice consumes all that is green and fair? Draw your steel, and let the echo of elven blades ring with yours, or be judged a coward in the fading light of the Valar.
You claim there is no such force... Behold. A number beyond reckoning, bred to destroy the world of men. You must join with them.
To every man his part. Valour in arms is yours, and you win high honour thereby. Slay whom I name as enemies, and be content.
Indifference serves no purpose now. Align with Isengard, or drift into irrelevance.
The world of men will burn. March with the Uruk-hai and see it so.
Who now has the strength to stand against you and Isengard? The Free Peoples, lord, are ready to fall.
The old world will burn in the fires of industry. We have work to do.
You have opposed the will of the White Wizard long enough. Pride has served its term. Let service be your next purpose.
You will serve Orthanc and assail the enemies of the new order. Know that your sovereignty is only tolerated as long as you remain obedient.
I will permit you the indulgence of opposition no longer. Resistance agains the rule of Order and Might is futile. Let this be your purpose instead: to crush its enemies.
I do not require thy love, only thy soldiers.
The storm does not spare the still stone. The war will find your borders soon enough. Better to stand with those who still fight for the light.
We bleed while you stand still. Join us, not for our sake, but for your own survival. For if we fall, you are next.
Friendships untested are no better than silence. Take up arms beside us!
War is upon us, and we do not fight it alone. We call upon you, friend, to fulfill your part.
We have stood shoulder to shoulder in peace, now stand with us in fire. Prove our friendship in truth, not comfort.
You seek our ruin. Now you’ll seek it for others, at our word. This is your absolution
War has found you. Choose whose wrath you’ll weather.
We’ll have your swords...willing or otherwise. Take up arms in our name and earn your survival.
It is a long-anticipated day, for the Lord of all Middle-Earth has deigned to grant thee service in His war.
Lugbúrz is aware that there are enemies that we share. It is within thy best interest to assist us in their downfall.
To fight side-by-side with the true Númenórean lords is an honour. Thou must stand beside the orc masses, but take comfort knowing that they watch over thee.
The Dark Lord calls upon thee now, for the time has come. The West will fall, one by one.
It is time to sate thy bloodthirst. To fight alongside His armies is a privelage, and one I hope thou willt not deny.
The armies are marching out to war as we speak. He has called all of His allies to war, and now He demands thy presence. Do not be left behind.
Thou art fodder in the mind of the Master, but He still has need of thee. Scrape together thy chipped blade and rusted armour, for war has come.
Pick up thy measly iron and form up. The Master has called thee to war.
There are worse dregs that serve the Eye in His wars, yet I feel a certain disdain enlisting thee...
Listen close, you lot. Here's the deal... Our blades for yours. Simple.
We got the numbers and we're not afraid to bleed for a fight. You want our blades when trouble knocks? Then we want yours in turn.
We're not keen on waiting for some pointy-eared rats or meddling men to come smashing down our walls. Let's stand together and rip apart whatever filth dares crawl against us.
Ride to your fortress. Let your legions come forth.
There is plenty of man-flesh for the both of us, here. Have at it, lad!
No point fighting alone when we could be smashing skulls side by side. Say the word, and we fight as one.
You think yourself high and mighty, wrapped in fine steel and elvish airs. But your time's run dry. Join our war, or we'll crack your bones and burn your lands.
If you march at our side, you keep your heads on your shoulders a bit longer. Maybe even eat proper.
Maybe you won’t be the ones getting gutted if you join our ranks. What say you, high folk?
The war-horn of the Rohirrim calls. Our enemies gather like crows to a carrion field. Pledge your sword to our cause, and let us meet them with steel.
Rohan needs every strong arm and stout heart it can muster. Will you answer the call to defend the free peoples from this rising tide of evil?
Will you ride with the Rohirrim, stand shoulder to shoulder in the shield-wall, to earn renown in this dark hour?
When dawn comes, I will bid men sound Helm's horn, and I will ride forth. Will you ride with me then?
Ride out with me! Ride out and meet them! For death and glory!
The West is in peril, as our enemy unleashes his reckless hate. Let this be the hour where we draw swords together!
The horn of Rohan sounds a call for aid. Answer it with fire and fury, or be forever stained by cowardice. Let your actions speak louder than words.
Your hearth is warm now, but the fires of war will soon reach even your halls. Only spear and blade can now turn back the tide of darkness, ere it is too late.
Can you call yourself warriors, if you stand aside and cower, while the Westfold burns and children are slain without mercy?
A call to arms! Your bows would make great work alongside our scimitars.
In the desert both the viper and the scorpion attack with venom. Woe to him whom they attack together.
Will you join us, at the turn of the tide?
Strike against our enemies and you shall be rewarded by the Black Serpent.
We wish to share the killing blow! Come, much blood must be spilled.
Distant are the lands of our enemies. A journey worth sharing. We extend an invitation to you, friend.
We must set aside our feud. There are greater enemies whose boots should be buried in the sands.
We will get this over with. A mutual enemy deserves destruction. Will you join us?
Can you make yourself useful and kill something worth killing?
They laugh at us. They will not laugh when their villages burn. Join us and make it so.
They spill our blood and take our children. You have hate in your heart too, I see it. Share our anger.
You've watched from afar, but the fire spreads. Stand with us or be caught in the blaze.
For too long, we've suffered their cruelty. Join our war. Free us from their grip.
Friendship’s not just words. It’s blade and breath.
You called us kin when skies were calm. Call us kin now, when the storm breaks.
We offer you a place in the storm. Refuse, and face its fury.
The ground you scorned now shakes with war. March with us, or be buried beneath it.
You called us beasts. Then be our hound. War is here.

diplomacy_strings_string_demand_single_p.value_original: For the upkeep of the defences that shield all lands, not least your own, a levy of gold is now due. See that it is rendered promptly.
Ever we bear the brunt of the chief hatred of the Dark Lord, for that hatred comes out of the depths of time and over the deeps of the sea. It is unjust that we should receive no support.
By the blood of our people are your lands kept safe; and war drains not only resolve, but our treasury also. We require you to share this burden, if you have the means.
A contribution to our treasury would be most fitting, ensuring the continued defence that benefits all lands of the West.
The defence of the West drains our coffers, and any support you might offer would greatly strengthen our shared resolve and the shield that protects us all.
A timely subsidy of coin from your domain would aid us greatly in maintaining that vigil which guards even your own borders from the Enemy.
Do you think the vigilance of the White Tower comes without cost? Your coffers are full while ours are strained by war. Pay what is due, or learn that we have means to collect our debts.
Your treasury is overspilling with ill-gotten gold, while we must maintain expenses to keep the Shadow at bay. Render what is due!
Your lack of commitment to the cause of the West has been noted. To compensate for your deficits in men and honour, a tribute in gold will be levied.
Right then, let's be blunt. Our forges burn hot, but the coffers are running a wee bit dry. A subsidy o' gold would keep us hammering.
Look, laddie, we're not beggars. But these are grim times. A bit o' gold now, and we'll remember ye in times to come.
It's a simple matter, really. Our work benefits ye. A subsidy will see the work continue. We both prosper; what's not to like?
Blast it all, it galls me to be here like this. But the mines have been lean, and the shadow stretches long. Lend us your wealth, and we'll make it worth your while.
Lords and Ladies, a word if you please. Our coffers are thinner than a goblin's beard. A wee bit o' your gold would see us right and your investment well protected.
Aye, times are lean, and I ain't one for beggin'. But a bit o' gold now strengthens the mountain against those who’d trouble ye later.
I've not got all day to stand around. A subsidy for our troubles is what we are here for, and ya better cough it up!
Now, I don't wanna sound like a mugger, but ya gotta hand over some coin. Won't ask nicely next time.
Open your coffers and hand over a fair tribute. This is not a request, understand?
All of this golden armor was quite costly. We expect some recompense.
This tribute from you will sate the golden hordes. For now.
In order to carry out war, three things are necessary: gold, gold, and yet more gold.
It would be just if our treasure-hoards were equal in size. A payment to my Chieftain will make them so.
The men of the West will not be conquered without a force well equipped and well trained. Each coin from you is another of them slain.
Give us this payment such that the golden hordes march to glory once more!
You spend your coin on frivolity and debauchery. Give it here. Witness what power gold may bring.
What need have you for wealth and fortune? Give your coin to those who know how to spend it!
You have less sense in management of a treasury than a goblin! Give us your gold, we'll put it to better use.
Our coffers, alas, reflect the fading glory of this world; a measure of your wealth, transferred to our care, would enable us to better weather the storms gathering on the horizon.

Though our needs are few and our desires fewer, the maintenance of these borders strains even our resources; consider then a contribution of gold, a boon for all free peoples against the Shadow that stirs.
The trees remember ages past, and even they now feel the chill of a harsh winter; a donation of gold would ensure that spring returns to this realm, and that its protectors are sustained.

The long years have witnessed both joy and sorrow, and now a new challenge faces us. With a modest grant of gold, we could better maintain the watch against those who disturb the forest, ensuring a safer path for all who travel it.

The weaving of fate has brought us to your door, seeking solace not only in friendship but in need. Natho ven! A contribution of gold would enable us to reinforce the protections of our borders, for the sake of peace in these lands.
Like the deep roots of ancient trees that draw sustenance from the earth, so too does our realm require nourishment. Surely, the wellspring of your generosity is as deep as the sea?
Let us not pretend this is a negotiation. The gold will be delivered, an acknowledgement of your debt to those who guard the borders while you sit idle.
While we preserve all that is fair, our ancient treasure-halls are depleted. I trust you understand the gravity of this matter, and will not force my hand further to seek what is due to us.
The coffers of our realm run low, depleted by unseen hands and shadowed creatures. Consider a levy for the vigilant watch we keep against the encroaching dark, a duty you seem unwilling to share.
Isengard has borne the burden of order. Compensation is not a demand. It is balance.
Stability must be sustained. If you intend to dwell in it, you will contribute to it.
Independence is not without price. Pay it, or forfeit such illusion.
Your loyalty to Isengard has been noted. Now it must be manifest, in coin, as in conviction.
The friendship of Saruman does not alone fuel forges or provision legions. Payment is due.
If you would remain among our favoured, act accordingly. The treasury of Orthanc awaits your answer.
Your hostility towards Isengard does not excuse obligation. Coin is but the first of many costs.
Even defiance has a ledger. Yours is now called due. Whether to preserve your walls or to purchase the delay of inevitability, you will pay.
You oppose us, and still the debt accrues. Render payment, or be reckoned by other means.
We ask for only that which was promised to us. A fair settlement... a meagre share of your great wealth.
Give this payment and help shape the outcome of our struggles. Refuse, and you may one day pay a higher toll...one set by others.
The coin we ask is not tribute. It is the price of the peace you’ve known while we've bled.
We ask a measure of silver to meet the needs that peace alone cannot answer. Let this be a gift given freely, though asked in earnest.
Our coffers strain, friend, and still we stand the line. We have need of payment to arm, to stand, to endure.
The darkness we hold at bay has drained more than steel and will. If you call us friend, let your gold speak too.
You can finance your own survival, or we can collect in steel.
The path of enmity is well-worn between us. A payment now may yet stay our ire.
Deliver the sum demanded, for we already have reason to take more than gold.
The riches, as some would call them, that thy land posesses are sought after far and wide. Let it be known that Sauron the Great lays claim to them, lest any other should try to take them.
It is the decree of the Master, Sauron the Great, that a tithe be collected from thy treasury.
The armies of the Eye must be maintained. A meager donation, nay, a pittance, is all that we require of thee.
The Lord of the Black Land once again requires tribute. Thou art a wise ally, and I trust that thou hath what He demands ready?
Thy land is a rich one indeed! There are lords in the tower who are jealous of thy wealth. Perhaps their envy could be appeased?
The friendship of the Lord of all Middle-earth must be maintained, and not let lie still. Surely, this was known to thee.
I do not see the worth in thy land. It is ugly and barren. Yet I am told that riches fill thy halls. It would be in thy best interest to deliver them to us.
Orc raiders eagerly stand outside thy walls, within thy lands, and hidden amongst thy serfs. A sum of gold might convince them to withdraw...
I have no time for games, little lord. Turn over thy wealth, and suffer not the ire of the Black Council.
You're not friend, you're not foe. Fine. But only coin keeps it that way.
Our lands have rules. Pay up, or the rules change.
Everyone pays. Some with coin, some with screams and blood. You pick.
A bit of coin keeps the knives sharp.
I'm building a new warcamp. Give me some coin.
You need hands, we got ‘em. You need blades, we swing ‘em. A little coin keeps it that way.
Pay what you owe us, or we take twice that in blood. Either way, we'll collect.
You’ve taken, you’ve stolen, you’ve killed. Now you pay. Give what’s owed, or I'll carve it out of you.
Orcs watch. Orcs wait. And Orcs take. Pay up, or find out what happens when we stop waiting.
Your lands prospered while our fields burned. Gold must flow, a blood-price paid for the spear-din you avoided.
Your coffers swelled fat while we faced the shadow. Empty them now, in tribute, a king's ransom for peace.
Our strength is your strength, and Rohan's needs are plain. A subsidy will aid our recovery, allowing us to remain vigilant against our adversaries. Remember, a strong Rohan benefits all.
Grim days have fallen upon the Mark, leaving our granaries low and our armouries strained. Ere the winter winds howl, grant us this boon, and Rohan will forever remember your generosity.
Riders of the Mark stand ever vigilant, but vigilance demands provision. A king’s gold given freely ensures our swords stay sharp, and our horses strong, for the common good.
We have bled freely defending this land, and our stores are diminished. I ask now, not as a right, but as a plea from a friend: grant us a share of your wealth to rebuild.
The graves of my riders cry out for recompense. Let your wealth silence them. A debt is due, a shield-tax to Rohan's crown, lest a greater price be demanded in blood.
Gold is the tongue of peace, but steel is the language of defiance. Choose wisely which you offer, for Rohan's riders thirst to ride out once more.
I speak plainly. Your coffers will open, and the King of the Mark will be satisfied. Refuse, and a red sun will rise above your fields.
A token to the sands is required to keep the tumbleweeds at bay.
Give us your coin. Lest we steal it anyway.
A tribute? A gift? We care not what you call it, but we demand your coin all the same.
Friend! Surely an antidote to our poisoned treasury is within your grasp?
We know you to be courageous! Brave! But will we know you as generous?
Your coin is valuable within our bazaars. We require more of it.
You fill our treasury, so we won't fill your graves.
Only by appeasing the Black Serpent can you slither from his shade.
Coin is the only mend for a forked tongue.
We are not your enemies. A little gold would mean much, and we would remember the kindness.
Pay now, or pay later when the hills come calling.
You owe no blood. Fine. Then owe silver.
Friendship walks on two legs: Talk and tribute. We’ve heard the first. Now show the second.
We call you friend. Let this coin prove it, before others call you coward.
You sit warm by our fire, so toss in some wood.
We ask once. The elders demand gold. Do not make us take what is ours.
We hunger. Your fat cities spill gold. Share it, or we take it.
Our axes stay sheathed. For now. Fill our coffers with gold.

diplomacy_strings_string_demand_soft_mil.value_original: The Men of the West must move swiftly to counter the Enemy's designs. I trust you will see the wisdom in granting our armies passage through your lands for the common good.
For the effective prosecution of the war against the Enemy of all, the White City asks that our hosts be free to march through your domain.
We require the right of passage for our troops. It is known that our men march in good order, and will not be a burden for your lands.
Friend of the Dúnedain, would you not offer us the courtesy to let our hosts march through your domains? Our men are disciplined and will treat your people with due respect.
Speed is our ally against the encroaching darkness. We come to you as friends, requesting leave for our soldiers to traverse your lands, that we may reach the foe before his designs mature.
For the greater good of all Free Peoples, we trust you will open your roads to the Men of the West, that we may strike where the Enemy is weakest.
Our armies will march through your domain to meet the Enemy. Obstruction will be viewed as aiding our foe, and dealt with accordingly.
There is no time for courtesy, as war encroaches even upon your lands. We only ask this once: grant our armies passage, or be swept away.
Would you be a hindrance to the Men of the West, one who aids the Enemy? No longer can our valiant soldiers be confined by petty borders.
Let us through.
There are elves and goblins that need a smackin'. Allow our armies to march there.
We've no quarrel with you, but with those on your other side.
Aye, I hate to ask, but we're in a right pinch. We need to move troops through yer territory, and quickly, so would ya mind lettin' us through?
Listen here, friend. We need passage through your lands for a company of our warriors.  We'd be in your debt, and not one easily forgotten.
Us dwarves aren't so keen on roamin'. Please make it easier for us, as a friend.
Right then, hear me out. Your lands stand 'tween us and goblin-scum, and we'll be marchin' through, like it or not.
We need to pass through yer lands. Would you rather our axes swing t'wards you?
We need to get to the mountains. Don't care for the piles of wood you call your home.
We march for leagues unending in our campaigns. Surely you will not turn us back now?
My golden hordes desire passage. Pray you grant it, lest they be loosed upon your lands.
Our war drums echo on the winds as we march ever to glory. We seek not respite in your lands, merely freedom of passage.
Honoured friend, gaze upon our hosts! They wish to grace your land with splendour in their passing, and return with glory. Do not let them down.
I grant you my finest blade in trust. I bid that you run me through with it, should our men cause trouble in your lands.
One day we will pillage the lands of our foes. When that day comes, I pray you will let us pass.
The clans have business in your lands and beyond. Do not provoke their ire, lest your land become one that we burn too.
Stepping one foot in your wretched lands pleases us not, but it must be done. Our foes lay far away.
Hinder not the golden hordes as they traverse and swiftly exit your afouled lands. It will not be a pleasant journey.
The long rivers of time carry us all downstream, whether we will it or not. To refuse passage is to dam the flow, risking that which might otherwise be avoided in these troubling days.
Let not pride or suspicion cloud your judgment. The whispers of unrest grow louder, and shared passage in times of need is a safeguard against the rising tide of shadow.
We ask not for hospitality, but for the grace of swift passage. Should the encroaching gloom thicken, a bridge between our realms may be all that stands against the night.
Our scouts report a growing disturbance; the Shadow stirs from its slumber, and we cannot ignore its hateful presence. Allow our soldiers to pass so that they may stand with you against any threat.
Tôl alagos. A storm gathers on the horizon, threatening to engulf us both. Lend us the use of your paths, that we may aid in holding back the flood.

The winds whisper of unrest beyond our borders; shadows lengthen where once the sunlight danced. Grant us passage through your lands, so that we might stand as a bulwark against the encroaching night.
The light of the Eldar dims, even as the Shadow lengthens. We shall pass through your lands, and woe betide any who hinder us.
Your borders now lie on the precipice of shadow. Open them to our warriors, or be swept away like leaves in a storm.
The tapestry of fate is fraying, and our path now leads through your forest. Let no whispering dissent stay our hosts, lest our blades cut through the thicket of resistance.
I have seen the movements of a great many hosts through the Palantir. Give my army leave through your lands to meet them on the field.
The old world is fading, as are the old ways of war. We must look beyond our borders now, to meet the enemy wherever he is weak. Do you not see wisdom in this?
There are movements abroad now against which the old allies and policies will not avail us. The forces of Isengard, marching across your domains, will grant safety and order.
My esteemed ally, the shadow lengthens, and a new power rises in the East. Surely, you perceive the utmost need to unite against this darkness, and will let my hosts march through your domains?
Is it not just that we, as old friends, grant each other the trust to tread our lands? I ensure you, my troops are disciplined and will inflict no harm.
I beseech you, friend, have I not ever shown you the utmost trust and respect? Let our cooperation extend beyond borders, for the good of all.
The gears of war grind ever onward, heedless of sentiment and borders. Refusal would be folly, as casting oneself between mill-stones: your very bones will be ground to dust.
I trust you perceive that this is hardly a request. Swing open the gates for my fighting Uruk-hai, or witness the devil-fire of Orthanc blasting them asunder.
The steel-tide of order and progess must sweep through your petty domains, ever onwards. Give way, or be swept aside.
We ask the courtesy of passage. If the battle passes through your lands, better with our shields than your homes unguarded.
If your gates open now, we strike first and hold strong. If not, we both risk a war fought in our own hearths.
Grant us leave to pass, not out of debt, but out of wisdom.
Your border is not a wall to us, rather it is a bridge between kin. Keep it open.
Our riders come not as conquerors, but as wardens of our shared peace. Open your roads to us.
Grant us this right of passage, that we may keep danger from both our doorsteps.
You will grant us passage, or face what follows when the road is taken, not given.
This path will be ours, whether paved with consent or cleared with force.
The road lies before us. Whether it opens or breaks beneath us...your choice decides the manner, not the march.
This decree comes direct from Lugbúrz. It grants us the right to traverse thy lands. Sign here to accept it, for we await passage already.
We demand access to thy lands, and in return grant thee access to ours. A fair trade, is it not?
Does the idea of orc masses freely roaming thy lands fill thee with glee?
I bear no love for the foul orc masses, yet they have work to do. Thou need not treat them, but thou must let them into thy lands.
The legions of the Eye have business to attend to in lands across thy own. We ask for passage, in good spirit, as is our right.
We would cross into thy land, lord. In due respect to our lasting and beneficial friendship, we request thy approval.
The armies of the Eye will traverse thy lands. This is our demand for thy blessing, but know that we are loath to be denied.
My Master has respect for thee, for He asks for permission to enter thy lands. I have no such respect.
The Lord of the Black Land requests entry, now. Though He feigns respect by asking, I will put up no such posturing.
The snaga scouts tell me our path lays in your direction. Do not harass us as we follow it.
Listen up, maggots. Our warbands need to march, and your lands are in our way.
Open your paths, let us through, and we’ll make sure your enemies get what's coming.
Open up that big gate of yours and let us in. We'll move at night and be swiftly out of your sight.
We don't want any favours, just an open road. We get through, and you get protection.
We got armies moving, and your lands sit in our path. Let us through, and the blood runs the right way.
Stay out of our way as we cross your lands, if you don't want your guts spilled and your blood drunk.
We've got no time for high folk nonsense. We march, and you'll keep away, or you'll lose your throats.
Let our fighters through, and maybe we won’t have to carve our own path... through your corpses!
A shadow lengthens across the land, and we ride to meet it. Grant our host swift passage, that we might yet turn the tide.
The hour is late, and the foe encroaches on our borders. Let our riders pass unimpeded, for the fate of Rohan, and perhaps more, hangs in the balance.
I ask passage for our riders, that we may meet the foe where they mass, and break their lines ere they reach our homes
The shadow lengthens across the Riddermark. Grant us passage, friend, so that we might meet the foe head-on, and buy time for our people.
Our enemies gather, and war is brewing even outside of our lands. We beseech you, open your borders, that our riders may swiftly answer the call to battle.
Grant our host swift passage; Rohan's need is dire, and by your aid, we might yet turn the tide.
We ride through your lands. Let no man stand against us; lest he be trampled under our hooves.
The Eorlingas ride to war, a storm of spears and hooves that break all in their way. I only ask this once for your consent to pass through your lands.
The hour is grim, and our need great. Make way for Rohan, or we shall cleave our own road.
Circumstances permit that we venture past the sands. Allow us to pass through yours.
Our army must move from water to water. Will you show us the way across your lands?
We have enemies across your chartered lands. Allow us passage, and give us a map to lead the way.
We march to meet the enemies of the Eye. For his glory, let us pass.
Our troops wish to feel soil under their boots and between their fingers. Will you give them that opportunity?
We are far from home. You could ease us by harbouring camps to rest.
Our soldiers are locusts. Allow them to pass, and they will not swarm.
Give us leave to pass, or find a razed city along the way to our destination.
Our soldiers want to kill. If you are not as stupid as you look, best let them pass, before they find easier prey in your lands.
Grant us safe passage, let us pass unharmed, and we will not trouble your lands.
The strawheads must pay. Lend us the road to reach them, and no blood will spill on your soil.
We raid. Let us through. Spare your lands.
Now open your gates. Our war needs room to breathe.
Your paths are known to us. Let our feet walk them now to strike what threatens us both.
We march where the wind calls. We seek passage, nothing more.
We got nothing to lose, and all the land to gain. Step aside.
Roads run where we will them. Deny us, and the hills will answer in smoke and scream.
Either your gates open, or your walls come down.

diplomacy_strings_string_demand_vassal_d.value_original: The hour is late, and the strength of the West must be gathered. We require an oath of fealty, that your people may find protection and purpose beneath the White Tree.
We extend the honour to be a branch of the White Tree. In exchange you must entrust your roots to us, so that your people may blossom as ours do.
Alone you will not stand against the Shadow. To ensure the common defence, your realm is to pledge your arms and your people to the heirs of Númenor,
The time for petty sovereignties is at an end. You will bend the knee and swear your allegiance to us, or your lands shall know the price of defiance against the rightful authority of the White Tree!
By the blood of Elendil, you will kneel before the White Tree, or be broken beneath its roots. It is for you to choose.
Behold! The blood of Elendil still runs true in us, and as the Númenóreans of old, we shall unite these lands, or lay waste to those that oppose us!
There is no mightier shade than that of a mountainside. Livin' in our shadow is mutually profitable.
There's no shame serving in the mansions of great mountain kings.
Swear fealty, this be yer best way out.
Yer head in a bow or rollin' on the floor. Don't matter to me what you pick.
This be yer last chance to have a shred of honour.
I suggest you join us, or be ready for a taste of Dwarvish steel.

diplomacy_strings_string_demand_vassal_e.value_original: My empire is made of many proud, strong warrior clans. We would honour you, if you would join us.
The golden dragon stands ready to spread fire across all lands. Will you be carried beneath its wings?
The Lord of Mordor calls upon us. Bind yourselves with Rhûn and partake in great glory.
Like the great fire worms of the mountains, I stand proud over you. It would be wise to kneel lest I bare steel fangs.
The might of Rhûn is measured in its warlords. If you do not submit to their will, you will surely feel their ire.
A fool sees his death looming ahead and rejects his path to avoid it. Prove that you are no fool.
Pride is a fine cloak, but it offers little warmth against the rising chill. Let your people find shelter beneath my protection; swear fealty to the Firstborn.
Your wisdom is evident, but the shadows lengthen in your path. Offer your allegiance, and together we will ensure your light does not extinguish.
The boughs of your house have grown thin; seek shelter within the deep roots of mine. Swear fealty, and let your strength bolster our own against the encroaching dusk.
Your future, like a leaf in the wind, now falls under our boughs. Bend your knee, and swear fealty to the Firstborn, or be diminished beneath us.
The grace of the Eldar surpass all that your kind may ever achieve. Bend the knee, or be broken like a dry twig beneath the winter frost.
And now at last it comes. You will give me allegiance freely! In place of the your lord you will set up a King. And I shall not be dark, but fair and terrible as the Morning and the Night!

diplomacy_strings_string_demand_vassal_i.value_original: Behold my Ring of power, for I am Saruman Ring-maker. Bow before the power of Isengard.
Isengard offers rule and knowledge. Bend the knee, and find your place in the new order.
Long have you wandered without banner or bond. Vassalage is not surrender, it is survival with purpose.
Emrace the power of Isengard, or embrace your own destruction.
There is but one path to escape from ruin: Join the rising power, lest you be crushed beneath it.
The Palantir of Orthanc reveals your destiny...to serve Isengard, and in doing so, survive the fall of the old age.

diplomacy_strings_string_demand_vassal_m.value_original: Let this be the day your people join something greater. Not as conquered, but as kin.
Let our banner shelter yours. In fealty, you gain our sword and shield, and we, your steadfast oath.
Do not bend your knee in fear, but in foresight. Swear fealty, and walk in step with history’s march.
Swear fealty and preserve what remains...or refuse, and be unmade. There will be no third road.
Accept our yoke, or be swept away like leaves before the storm.
The world you knew is ended. What remains lies in our shadow. Bind yourselves to us, or be cast from the light that still lingers.
I have come bearing tidings. My Master demands thy servitude, and His command cannot be ignored.
Thy kingdom is weak and thy men falter. If thou wouldst survive this war, it would suit thee to kneel now, before the choice is lost.
What a petty kingdom. It would serve both thine and my Master's interest if thou wouldst relinquish thy crown.
Bow now, wretch! Bow before the might of Sauron the Great, lest thy blood water the graves of thy kingdom's children!
The Eye demands thy servitude at once. His will cannot be opposed: submit now or perish.
Thy time has come and passed, and thy strength is waned. I would press my heel to thy chest, if thou were any greater lord, ha!

diplomacy_strings_string_demand_vassal_o.value_original: Swear loyalty, or we'll carve it into your bones.
You’ve no teeth, no tribe, no strength. Best you serve beneath ours before someone worse comes knockin’.
Your land's already in our shadow. Might as well wear our chains proper.
Submission is your only course. You face slaughter if you don't kneel.
Your banners will fall, your walls will crumble. Fealty is your one escape.
Bow now, or we rip your banners down and drown your halls in blood. Maybe your young don’t get fed to the wargs.

diplomacy_strings_string_demand_vassal_r.value_original: I, King of the Mark, offer you this choice: swear fealty to Rohan, and find strength in our shield-wall. Refuse, and stand alone against the coming storm.
I offer you kinship and protection, to ride among the mighty Eorlingas. In return, I demand your oath, your service as a vassal. Choose wisely, for the fate of your people hangs in the balance.
Rohan stands as the last bastion against the encroaching darkness. Swear now to be my vassal, to fight when we fight, and your land shall find protection in our strength.
Speak plainly: will you be shield-thane to Rohan, or will you be crushed beneath the hooves of the Rohirrim? Delay is defiance.
The choice is thus: become my vassal, or feel the full weight of Rohan's anger. This is no request, but a king's decree, etched in steel and blood.
Your domains are now forfeit to Rohan. Refuse, and know the wrath of our riders until none remain to defy us.

diplomacy_strings_string_demand_vassal_s.value_original: There are many tribes that make up the deserts and sunlands of Harad. You would fit in amongst them.
We offer an oasis among a desert of death, in exchange for your blade.
In the shade of our palms you shall find the same salvation that we have imposed on others.
There was once a mighty jungle kingdom that once refused to serve us. Their temples lie in ruins now.
If you do not wish your lands raided and your men enslaved, then your only choice is servitude.
We require your lands for trade routes, cities for caravan posts, and ports for havens. Bend the knee, else we take them by way of desert fury.

diplomacy_strings_string_demand_vassal_w.value_original: No banners fly forever. Raise ours now, or face the wind alone.
Get off your horse and kneel.
You call us beasts. Now serve the beast, or feel its teeth.
Choose: Shame in life, or silence in death.

diplomacy_strings_string_generic_offer_d.value_original: The days darken, and there must be no delay. I seek your agreement in this endeavour.
Greetings. The times are urgent, and pleasantries must be brief. I come with a proposal from the White Tower that warrants your serious consideration.
I bring to you matters of urgence. Hear me, lord of these lands, and consider wisely.
I trust you will see the wisdom in acceding to Gondor's request in this, for it serves us both.
To ensure the prosperity and safety we both cherish, certain measures are now essential. Your cooperation is expected.
Let there be no misunderstanding of our resolve in this matter. For the good of your people, heed this demand.
For the good of all that is fair, I propose this arrangement, and would gladly hear your assent.
Time presses, and trusted friends must rely upon one another. I put this charge to you, knowing your heart is with us, and expect your swift agreement for the sake of all we defend.
Our friendship is a beacon in these shadowed lands, and it is in that spirit I come. Yet I must insist upon your compliance in this matter.
My esteemed friend, the burden of these days falls heavily upon us all. For the sake of the West, I must ask that you lend your strength to this vital course of action.
As true allies of the West, your support in this particular endeavour is required, if our common front against the Enemy is to hold. I am confident you will not fail us.
Not lightly do I make these demands of you, for I value your sovereignty and the goodwill you have shown us in past days.
Though there is no love between your kind and mine, the situation demands compliance in this matter.
Even your limited understanding must grasp the necessity here. Do not try my patience further; fulfill this demand, and perhaps your lands might yet see another season.
I have no time for petty haggling. You will do as the lords of my realm bid, or face the inevitable consequences. Choose swiftly.
Consider this not a request, but a decree from one who holds the power to enforce it. Your obedience in this matter is demanded.
The eye of the White Tower sees further than most. This demand is but a necessary step on a path already laid out by forces beyond your understanding.
It is known that your own counsel is oft amiss. Perhaps you will heed wisdom, when it is presented so clearly by those who bear the true sight of things.
Hear me. A deal to bring prosperity to both our coffers.
My foots turned to stone by way of travel here. I come far, so that you may hear my plea.
Do ye have any ale? No? Well, I've some right here if ye agree to this.
We left our mountain-hall for this. Ye owe us some respect. Say yes.
The seven houses of the dwarves thank ye in advance.
Mind ye, ye ought not refuse this.
Say yes, such that the world can grow old and the days of our people can rest.
We've prepared a feast for when you agree, friend.
Dwarves are proud, but we know when we need aid.
It be a stout and well-armed son of Durin that holds back the Enemy. Friend, make him so.
We know now that we need yer aid, lest the sons of Durin fall.
Will ye show wisdom and courage in accepting this, or are you not a friend of the dwarves?
You keep my beard short and cold, my fist brittle, and my locks white. We offer this out of need, not desire.
Yer heart reminds me of Moria. Prove that there's some light left.
Say yes so we can leave this Aulë's forsaken place.
The sooner ye agree, the sooner we ne'er need speak again.
Say yes, then get out of me face, before yer head rolls 'round on the floor.
If it's a hammerin' ye be seekin', refuse this deal.
A Chieftain of Rhûn calls upon you to accept this offer, that it may prove mutually fruitful.
Our Chieftains expect your acquiescence to the terms of the offer laid before you.
The traveler to Rhûn fathoms not the vast expanse before him, nor do I fathom why you have not yet agreed.
It is not your place to question these terms. It is your place but to accept them.
Rhûn demands this be done. Will you meet its demand? Or will you defy the will of the hordes?
Believe not that you have a choice here today, ere my guards' glaives be coated red.
We make this offer to you who is a friend of Rhûn. Show us your friendship in kind by accepting it.
This offer do I present to you, its terms fitting for our stations. How will you respond?
One who is a friend of Rhûn need not turn away from these terms.
I ask this of you in good faith. Respond in kind, that we may both share in this boon.
We would seek accord this day, if you would but honour the terms of this agreement.
It would suit us that you agree to this proposal, and we will both likewise share in its bounty.
Heed this, wretch. Show us you have even a shred of rectitude.
We do not expect you to have the sense to accept this offer willingly, and so we demand it!
The Chieftains care not for your opinion on the matter. They only care for your assent to it.
Accept this proposal, or your head can be returned in a box to your vile lands. It matters not.
My guards, and I, in truth, would have you defy me, to give us justification for bloodshed. Enemy of the Rhûn, do you consent to our demands?
Your wretched lives are your own this day, but I expect you to agree to my demands.
The blight of our forest bids me delay no further. I demand your agreement in this endeavour.
Le suilon. The hour is late for courteous speech. I come with a proposal from the Wood-elves that demands earnest consideration.
By the whisper of trees and the song of birds we have descried matters of great import. May you judge our proposal wisely.
Surely you comprehend the wisdom of this counsel, for it would benefit both our people.
I greet you, and urge you heed my counsel. For the darkness is ever growing, and lesser desires must be put aside.
The lore-masters have designed this treaty, that it may nourish both our people.
Mae govannen! I bring counsel from the Wood-elves, trusting in your wisdom and friendship.
Le a vellon. I come as friend, knowing your heart is true. Will you not lend your ear to my request?
Not lightly do I make demands of those I value as friends, yet necessity compels me. I hope this matter casts no shadow upon our lasting friendship.
As you show wisdom and understand the needs of our forest, I hope we may come to an accord that benefits us both.
Mae govannen! Friend of the West, I implore you consider the fading of the light and the growing shadow: lend us your hand in times of need.
If you would but lend me your ear, I would parley with you on behalf of the Forest, for your wisdom of lore is well-known and needed.
The Sindar haggle not with lesser kind. These are our demands: see them fulfilled at once.
Think it not a mere proposal, but an order from one who sees further and has more mastery of lore.
More wisdom have I gathered over the ages than your limited understanding could ever grasp. Heed thus my counsel, or learn the punishment for folly.
In the name of the Forest, we bid you consider well these claims that we urge, or be declared our foe.
As the elders speak, the children obey. Deem this not a suggestion, but a command.
Your fleeting existence is but a blink in the life of the Eldar. You may heed our counsel or find your insignificant life soon lost to time.
I acknowledge your limited understanding, so let me lay it out plainly: A wiser mind than yours has crafted this proposal, it merely requires your formal agreement.
Much have I desired to see you, mightiest king of western lands, to save you from the unwise and evil counsels that beset you! Is it yet too late?
You need not speak to me as to one of the fools that you take for friends. I have not come hither to be instructed by you, but to give you a choice.
The time for polite diplomacy is past; the time of action is at hand. I believe my vision aligns with your own, and I have an offer that may be of great interest.
Your neutrality in matters of politics is an illusion you can ill afford. Now is the time to reveal whether you are aligned with the new order, or against it.
Larger powers than you are now moving, and a new strategy must be forged. I trust you see the wisdom in acceding to Isengard's interests.
It is rare to find someone who can grasp the inevitability of progress. My offer promises power, a power that surpasses the petty squabbles of lesser races.
My old friend and helper, do you not approve of the high and ultimate purpose: Knowledge, Rule, Order; all the things that we have so far striven in vain to accomplish?
I greet you, most esteemed lord, and thank you for gracing me with an audience. I promise, I have brought an offer that is worth your valuable time.
Hail, o thrice-renowned son of great sires! I would deliver you from the ruin that draws nigh inevitably, if you ride upon this road which you have taken. Indeed I alone can aid you now.
Will you have an accord with me, and all the aid that my knowledge, founded in long years, can bring? Shall we make our counsels together against evil days, old friend?
My request is but a small one, compared to the power that a friendship with Isengard offers. Have I not ever been benevolent to you?
Would you heed the demands of Saruman, or would you be cast from the pinnacle of Orthanc?
Consider well your position, offspring of a lesser race. The price for obstinacy is far greater than the simple concession I require. So, choose wisely.
A simple signature under this harmless proposal is all I demand. Ah, you are not capable of writing, I presume? Then a crude crisscross shall be sufficient.
This then is the choice before you: Aid me willingly, or elect the way of pain.
I have attempted to lay out this demand in the most simple terms for it to be comprehensible to one of your lesser kind.
A new power is rising. You may now join with that power and heed its demands, or fall together with the remnants of a bygone age.
What we ask is fair, and may serve you as well as us.
You know the world grows darker by the day. Help us maintain the light.
Grant this, and we may both find strength in it.
Say yes and show us that you see the world as it is.
Do this for us, and you may find us more inclined to remember your name in the gathering dark.
It is in your interests to acquiesce, for you have little to lose and much to gain.
Grant our request as a gesture between friends who understand the weight of trust and necessity.
We would not ask if the need were not great. You know us well enough to trust that.
We would not come to you if we doubted your wisdom. You know what must be done.
The weight of this age is not ours alone to bear. Help us carry it, and we shall not falter.
Let our friendship be proven once more in deed.
This is not a demand made in haste. It is the voice of a friend in need, and we trust it will not go unheard.
Grant this, or risk learning what we are willing to do without it.
Consider this demand a test of your judgment.
This is not a request...it is a chance. Take it, or let the road between us grow darker still.
Refuse, and you will pay a higher price. One you may not survive.
You gain nothing by spiting us. Agree, and you may yet avoid worse days.
We are done speaking softly. Grant this, or face the full measure of our wrath.
Hearken well. Sauron the Great deigns to offer thee terms, shouldst thou possess the wit to comprehend them.
Hear my demands, and be warned: I speak for the Black Council, and they follow the will of the Eye.
Read this, if thou would. It outlines the desires of Lord Sauron the Great, and the consequences of denying Him.
The Lord Sauron of Mordor has these demands for thee. Accept, and friendship is thine. Refuse, and things will not seem so well.
If thou would only accept these terms, I may be inclined to tell the Master of thy compliance.
Thou hath good manners. That is well, but only if thou hath also the mind to know when to submit.
If thou wouldst maintain friendship with the Dark Lord, dismiss not His demands.
I trust that these terms are agreeable? There is enough conviction in thee that I would not fleece thee on purpose.
The Black Council favours thee: our demands are fair and just, as they always are, but even more so to thee.
I trust thee, as thou art trusted by the Master. As such, thou should trust me and sign here.
Our demands are but a trifle for one so powerful and wealthy as thee. Surely, thou must accept.
Lord Sauron the Great desires just a small thing, the least of things, from thee.
Bow, spawn of lesser sires! The Lord of the Earth commands thy obedience, and I deliver His decree.
Shall I read off the list of demands from the Tower? I am told there are hardly any literate minds in thy lands...
There exists but two choices for thee: submit to my demands, or suffer the touch of the tormentors of Lugbúrz.
Most blades in the dungeons of Mordor are kept partly blunt and rusted, to the delight of our torturers. Keep this in mind with thy decision.
Sauron the Great does not suffer to have His demands rejected. Heed me well, for thy life hangs in the balance.
Thou need not read our demands. Accept and thou shalt live, deny and ruin will come to thy lands.
Choose this pact, or see which way the scales tip when our war-drums call.
No blood’s been spilled...yet. Agree, and keep it that way.
This one's a fair demand. The next one might come with fangs attached.
The terms are clear. You've got breath left...use it to agree.
You’re smarter than most. You’ll say yes. You will say yes.
Refuse, and we’ll remember. Not today. Not tomorrow. But when it stings most.
You’re one of the few we don’t spit at. Keep it that way. Pull your weight and say yes.
You're not doing us a favour here. This is the price of the fire we share.
We marched together, fed the same flame. You owe us more than silence. Answer loud, and answer yes.
We wouldn’t ask if we thought you were weak. But you’re not. So see this done.
We stood with you before, and we expect recompense. Call it duty, or call it debt.
We ask only once. Friends don’t need second chances.
Them's the terms, nothing more. Take it or get out of my sight.
See that Fell Beast? Borrowed him from Mordor, I did. He looks hungry. Best give me the right answer.
Looks like you got some meat on your bones. Shall I get to carving? Save yourself with a word.
We wasted enough words. Give us your answer before we give it for you.
Must be hard to speak when fear clogs your mind. Here, perhaps a knife at your throat will hep you say yes.
We spoke. We didn’t kill you. Generous, wasn’t it? Don’t waste it.
The Rohirrim do not treat needlessly, and demand to be taken heed, as we expect your agreement here.
There is no ill will between our peoples, and I have treated with you in good faith. I expect you to agree.
There is no time for delay. Rohan calls upon you, not in idle request, but in dire need.
Our realms stand apart, yet the shadow comes for us all. Rohan does not demand without cause.
Orcs roam freely across Rohan. The Westfold is burning. Your agreement would be our succour, for the hour is dire and our need is great.
When last I looked, I was the King of Rohan. I would suggest you heed my demand, lest you face the scorn of the Golden Hall.
We would see you agree to these terms, lord, for such is the way of friendship.
Rohan does not impress demands upon friends without grave circumstance requiring it. We are sorry, but we must insist.
I ask this of you as one sovereign to another, in friendship yet with firm resolve. Will you grant what is required?
Rohan calls upon you in this hour of need. Our enemy does not sleep, does not wait. What is your answer?
May you swiftly declare your response, friend, for delay is the ally of the enemy.
Friend of Rohan, I do not speak lightly when I say that our time is short. I would have your answer.
Agree to these terms and the Éored company outside will stand down. Reject them, and you will find them less friendly.
Wouldst thou agree? Or wouldst thou prefer a spear through thine heart?
You will yield what is owed, or face the wrath of the Mark. Choose swiftly, lest your delay be met with steel.
I will not waste breath on pleasantries. I do not ask, I demand. Make your choice before it is made for you.
This is the last time I speak before the war-horns of Rohan sound across the plains. What say you?
There shall be no mercy, no parley, only ruin for those who defy the Mark!
Say yes and we will suspend the smuggling for a short time.
I suggest you accept. Some of my chieftains would get the idea to slip poisonous serpents into your bed... while you are sleeping.
I would think you would desire a deal with the Black Serpent, rather than being bitten by him.
It is action that speaks to our chieftains, not hollow words. How will you speak to them?
It would be unfortunate if our smugglers were to expand operations in your lands. If you accept, however...
I have not mastered your strange language, so I assume whatever you respond will be an agreement, yes?
He that would call himself a friend of the Haradrim must trust the terms we present will not be a burden.
We must insist that you demonstrate your goodwill to Harad by agreeing to these terms.
The terms we present are appropriate for a friend of the Haradrim, and we ask you accept them earnestly.
As a friend of Harad you have our utmost respect. We wish to continue to build this relationship with another deal.
Already your people are esteemed on the bazaars. Let us close this negotiation, and you will be respected in the palaces also.
I have brought this gift of palm-fruit and cold water, friend. Now, in return, I bid you listen to these terms.
The corsairs have already finished mapping their raids against you, should you decline these terms.
Agree to my demands, and you might not be carried off in the middle of the night by an angry troll-man.
There is a torturer in Gobel Ancalimon I would be very pleased to introduce to you, if you voice your disagreement today.
There is a knife to your back, vermin. Take this deal and you live through the trap.
You're dead in the water if you even think of saying no to this deal.
A fate worse than death is saying no to the Black Serpent.
That omen speaks to you. It tells you to accept.
The terms are clear. Take them.
The hills have spoken. These are our terms.
Agree, and let's be done. I long for the hills already.
Show you've got the heart of the wilds within you, and agree.
Accept the terms, and show your word has weight.
Show us your strength by accepting our terms.
If there's friendship between us, let it show. Accept these terms.
What we ask is fair, and we expect it met. Friends don’t twist the hand that’s offered.
The path we've laid is not a hard one. Walk it, if you are indeed a friend of the hills.
You call the wildmen friends. Prove it now, take the terms.
Let your fire warm us both. Say yes.
We want it so. Or there will be war.
Here. Do this, and you won't feel the wrath of the wild. Not yet.
We demand this. You are weak. We are strong.
We don’t speak twice, and we don’t speak soft. Accept, or the next sound will be the ring of iron.
Refuse this if you want to see why they call us wild.
My terms are more than you deserve. Take them.

diplomacy_strings_string_generic_reject_.value_original: The Lord of Gondor is not to be made the tool of other men's purposes, however worthy.
Nay, other counsels may be found that are neither the webs of wizards nor the haste of fools. I have in this matter more lore and wisdom than you deem.
Ever your desire is to appear as a king of old, gracious and gentle. That may well befit one who sits in peace, but in desperate hours gentleness may be repaid with death.
Certainly your offer was made with fair intent, but we cannot survive on goodwill alone these days.
Our need is ever growing in these darkening days. I cannot lightly accept such an accord.
The White Tower bears many responsibilities, and its resources, though great, are not limitless. We cannot accede to every petition laid before us.
Alas, there are many schemes afoot, and for all your wisdom we cannot follow your guidance at this time.
Would that I lived in fairer times! But alas, I am pressed from all sides, and must delay decision on this matter.
Would that I could say yea! Yet duty binds me to refuse, for the path ahead is already chosen.
Your speech reflects upon your keen insight, as ever from you. Yet, for reasons of strategy I may not now unfold, we must choose a different way.
The foresight in your words is clear, and in fairer times, we would gladly assent. However, the present currents steer Gondor's ship by another star for now.
We cannot embrace your current course, but let not this divergence diminish the amity between us. Perhaps another season will see our paths align.
You think you are wise, yet for all your subtleties you have not wisdom. Do you think the eyes of the White Tower are blind?
Madness has befallen you, to think that the Lord of the Dúnedain would be made a puppet for your lowly purposes!
The White Tree stands tall, and bows not to your very command. There is no place for your insolence here!
Had you all the seven Seeing Stones, still you would be blind. Do you not see that your demands are shameless?
We did not come here to waste words in treating with one faithless and accursed. Begone!
As for your terms, we reject them utterly. Get you gone, for your embassy is over and death is near to you.
You can forget it. We won't be doing that.
By Durin, ye expected me to say yes to this? No.
The grumbling of our kin would deafen our ears if we said yes.
You have no honour. We have no interest.
Dwarves haven't got this far by saying yes to deals like this.
No. Next time, fill my belly with ale and coffers with coin before ye ask!
It pains us to say no to a friend.
To strike a deal ye must swing like an axe to stone. You've not hit gold this time, friend.
There's gold in yer heart. Not in your tongue today.
Don't mistake our refusal for disrespect, friend. We just can't.
Our hands are tied tighter than a goblin's purse strings. Regretfully, we must refuse yer offer.
Now, now, let's not get hasty. That's a bonny idea, but it needs a wee bit of adjustment, friend.
I'd rather trust all of them Woodelves than you! And I never trust an elf!
I'd sooner shave my beard with goblin steel! Get out of my sight before I decide to demonstrate dwarven hospitality with my ol' axe!
Your first mistake was coming to our sacred halls. Second, desecrating them with the sorry offer you set before us.
By Durin's beard, are you daft? Get out of my sight before I rearrange your face with me axe!
I'd sooner shave my beard with a dull axe. The answer, as you may have guessed, is a resounding no.
Is that all you've got, you witless whelp? I've seen goblins offer more for a rusty nail!
The clans will not be taken advantage of in this or any other way. Your offer is rejected.
You will find that the sons of Rhûn are not so easily convinced.
Though we are to the far East, we are not so naive to the ways of the world as to accept such terms.
Our proud reputation as fearsome folk would be tarnished by accepting terms such as these.
A dragon need not concern itself with the opinions of any other, for they burn in golden fire all the same.
As we rejected the words of the Blue Wizards, we likewise reject yours now.
Come now, friend. Surely you knew it was not possible for me to accept your terms even before you uttered them.
We cannot accept this proposal even from one such as you.
The dragon priests issue warning against your terms, friend. We are sorry to reject them.
You remain a friend of Rhûn, but the Chieftains have agreed your proposal is folly.
Even when it is you who brought the terms, I would rather be swallowed by the Sea of Rhûn than abandon the voice of reason.
While there is wisdom in your words, friend, Rhûn is on a different path.
I would rather Elves rule all the lands of this world than accept such an offer.
The desperate hour may require desperate measure, but none such hour has come to Rhûn.
Take your petulence away from my palace. These terms are better off presented to an ignorant valesman.
It is rare that opportunities are given to unite the chieftains outside of warfare. But now you united all in rejecting this proposal.
Ha! You really are that witless! The chieftains were right!
You insult the chieftains. You threaten my people with slavery and death. Choose your next words carefully, they may be your last as king.
While your purpose may seem true, our fates are woven from different threads; thus, we must decline your request.
I sense the shadows lengthen even as we speak. To cede what you desire would only embolden them further, and that is a risk we cannot take.
The lore-masters have long considered your proposal, and deem it ill-advised. Alas, we must reject.
Too bold is your speech in this late hour. It would be ill-advised to lightly agree.
Ever has the protection of our realm been our prime concern. As the shadows lengthen, we cannot entertain such daring ventures.
Truly, you speak with a righteous heart. But while you ponder mere years, the Firstborn think of ages of time, far beyond your comprehending.
I would that we were one in mind, but I oppose your counsels: for a man must speak as he sees, nor hide the truth that he believes, for any private cause.
Though my heart leans towards accord, a chill wind whispers caution through the eaves. We must, with regret, refuse your proposal.
Think not that my answer is given lightly, for it pains me to refuse such a generous spirit.
Though I admire your boldness, I cannot grant your wish at this time. Forgive this denial; circumstances beyond our control bind our actions.
Your words shine as bright stars, but the road ahead is shrouded in mist. I cannot grant what you ask.
It brings me sorrow that I may not take your hand in agreement, but the lore-masters issue caution, for your demands are bold.
Your words are as dry leaves scattered before the wind, meaning nothing to the ancient heart of this land. The Eldar bow to no mortal claim!
Stay thy uncouth tongue that spreads but the foul lies of Sauron, lest it shall taste the sharpness of Elven steel!
Your veiled lies are of no avail. The Firstborn treat not with henchmen of the Enemy.
A charming jest, little one, but my mirth expired centuries ago. I suggest you reconsider your boldness, if you would not forge your own demise.
The river of time has flowed long before your birth, and will continue after your unworthy end. Your brief insistence is scarcely a ripple.
Ah, so you presume the moth holds sway over the light that it circles. It bemuses me, but beware, for you may find yourself burned if you persist.
Your offer lacks both foresight and understanding. Seek wisdom elsewhere, and perhaps then you may return with something worthy of my time.
Perhaps I was foolish to think you wise and worthy of my time. Yet not foolish enough am I to accept such a proposal.
Your demands, while perhaps understandable from your limited perspective, are utterly impractical. The future belongs to those who embrace order and efficiency.
I see only the fading light of a bygone era in your words, a refusal to accept the inevitable. Sentimentality cannot be allowed to impede the forging of a new, stronger world.
While I acknowledge your concern, your path is that of the past. It would be wise to consider the future, and aid those that shape the dawning age.
Your request is quaint, but narrow-minded. Such lowly concerns are beneath those who understand the true order of the world.
Friend of Isengard, I ever value your counsel, but at times necessity must overrule friendship. I cannot now let my plans be disturbed.
I understand your disappointment, but my allegiance is to progress, to the forging of a future where the mind triumphs over the frailties of nature.
The world is changing, my friend, and I trust you have the wisdom to see that your suggestion would lead us astray from the path of order.
I lament that our objectives do not align, but the future will be written in steel and fire, not in antiquated appeals to honour.
Alas, my friend, your sentimentality holds little sway against necessity, for the gears of Isengard's industry are already turning towards a new age.
My wise friend, surely you see that the age of rash oaths and sentimental alliances is waning? Strength and efficiency are the chief virtues, and power is forged in furnaces of steel.
I know not why I have had the patience to speak to you. You give me brag and abuse. Go back to your huts!
I suppose you also want the Keys of Barad-dûr itself, and the crowns of seven kings, and the rods of the Five Wizards? You shall have naught!
I grow weary of this charade. Your demands are as hollow as your promises. Leave now, before I demonstrate the consequences of insolence.
Your demand is as amusing as it is pathetic. You cling to a past that is already dust, whilst I forge the future in furnaces of fire.
Did you truly believe such a paltry offering would sway the architect of a new age? Return to your derelict hovels, and leave the matters of the world to more potent minds.
Such naivete! It is a wonder your kind has survived this long. Insults to common sense, like this offer of yours, will not be tolerated in the age of metal that is to come.
Nay, I will have nothing of that sort. Good day!
