Even the very wise cannot see all ends. But I at least see agreeing to this would serve me naught.
Now is the winter of our discontent...with your terms, and with you.
The answer is no. Speak no more of it.
The matter is closed. Your welcome here is ended.
You try to build a bridge too far with such terms.
Your words were not without merit, yet the course you set is one we cannot follow.
No, I cannot. Let’s keep to the roads we know, and may they always lead us back to each other.
May our goodwill endure, even if our choices differ. I cannot agree with your terms today.
We walk beside you in spirit, but not in this endeavor. Our path lies elsewhere.
Were times less fraught, I might have accepted, but my people must tread carefully in these uncertain days.
It is not mistrust that stays our hand, but prudence. Such terms among friends would be unwise.
We will have no accord while your shadow lingers at our borders.
Your words are full of sound and fury, yet signifying nothing. I reject them, for never again will a shadow fall our lands.
You seek to bind us with words where force has failed. We will not be bound.
Your terms mask the face beneath. We see it, snarling and sneering, and we tell it no.
Your offers are ash, and your promises dust. Take them and flee this place while your life is still yours.
We speak to you in none but the tongue of war. Have at thee.
Thy proposal is rejected utterly. Waste not our time with such follies again.
My Master will consider no such thing. Thy persistence is wearisome.
Sauron's purposes are His own, and shall not be swayed by thy insignificant entreaties.
Know that Sauron the Great finds thy offer laughable and unworthy of consideration.
Sauron’s answer is this: nay. Thy desires are irrelevant; thy hopes, ashes.
The sight of the Eye extends far beyond thy limited understanding. Thou graspeth not thine insignificance.
I had hope that thou were not a fool. Do not prove me wrong again, for the sake of our friendship.
We cannot accept. Friendship with Sauron the Great will only get thee so far.
Not this time. There is merit in thy demands, but we cannot accept anything that does not put the Master's will first.
Thy time would be better spent elsewhere, I assure thee.
While thy offer amuses me, mortal, Sauron the Great hath plans beyond thy feeble imagining.
Thou hast not understood thy friendship with Sauron. He is to make demands of thee, not otherwise.
Begone. Thy words are filth, and thy presence an affront to Sauron’s gaze.
The agony! The pain! Oh, no, not my pain. I simply describe the remaining minutes of thy life after making such demands.
I would throw thee into the fires of Mount Doom for such ramblings.
Were thou one of my snagas, I would have had thee dismembered for such a demand.
Absolutely not. I tire of blithering, jabbering fools acting as emissaries of some lesser lords.
My ire is tested against thy foolish requests. Is it part of thy culture to swindle the hosts that would treat thee?
No deal. Fine by us. Less talking, more raiding.
No. And next time you send messengers, send ones you don’t mind losing.
Not now. Not while we smell fear. You need us. We don’t need you.
Even drunk on draught I'd say no to this!
We've no stomach for that kind of talk. Come back when you’ve got something worth bleeding for.
We heard your words, tasted the air...and it stinks of coward’s bargain. We pass.
You’ve earned our trust, but not our leash. This pact binds too tight.
A shame, really. We liked your offer. Almost made us forget we’re Orcs. Almost.
For both our sakes, we pass. Orcs need sharp teeth, and this would dull ours.
Doesn't sit right in the gut. Another time, maybe.
This move smells strange...tips the scales the wrong way. Not today.
I think not. Good ties are worth keeping. This deal risks fraying ‘em.
I don't take orders from maggots. Watch out if you want to keep your head.
Utter another word and you'll be meat for the fire, maggot.
You're lucky that we let you live. Step into camp again and you'll be stepping over your own corpses!
Eat shrakh and die, pinkskin!
Crawl back to your hole before we bury you in it.
I wonder if you'd be as brash when you're wearing your insides on the outside.
Lies come too often and too easily from stranger's lips. I cannot accept so swiftly.
As we speak, my thought goes to the people of Rohan, and to their ancestors long before me. For their sake I reject your offer.
There seems no benefit for Rohan in accepting your terms, so I must decline them.
Have patience. Not all is lost as we reject your terms. Go where you must go, and with hope!
Our road does not lead the same as yours. We have no quarrel with your folk, but neither do we have cause to entwine our fates.
Your folk have walked their own paths, far from Edoras. Your proposal is heard, but it shall not be accepted.
Rohan must stay its course this day, unwavering and resolute. You are welcome to return, friend, but alas, there will be no agreement here.
diplomacy_strings_string_generic_reject_.value_translated: Rohan debe mantener su rumbo hoy, inquebrantable y resuelto. Eres bienvenido a volver, amigo, pero, por desgracia, aquí no habrá acuerdo.

diplomacy_strings_string_generic_reject_.value_original: Fate goes as it must. I cannot twist it, even by request of friends.
There are times in which one friend must refuse another. I fear this is one such time, but I bid you good fortune hence.
It takes a great deal of bravery to refuse one's enemy, but a great deal more to refuse one's friend.
You know well the burdens that weigh upon a kingdom in war. Rohan cannot commit to this action, though our friendship remains unbroken.
You have ever been a friend of the Riddermark, yet Rohan must tread its own path in these dark days. We cannot take this course.
A lesser son of greater sires am I, but I do not need to lick your fingers. Turn elsewhither! But I fear that your voice has lost its charm.
You hold out your hand to me, and I perceive only a finger of the claw of Mordor. Cruel and cold!
This offer is as insulting as it is bemusing. You missed your path in life, you should have been the king's jester!
The wrath of Helm Hammerhand is known by legend in the Mark, as will be my wrath in response to such words.
The King of the Mark does not banter with a witless worm. I say no, and take my leave.
You speak of diplomacy, yet my people have known only war at your hands. Your offer is refused, and Rohan shall not suffer your presence further.
Disappointing to travel all this way to recieve this offer. We will say no.
Allow the sands of time to shift before asking us again. As it sits now, we can not accept this.
The chieftains have sent word, for they know from afar that you are here. They caution against your proposal, and so I must decline.
The winds do not blow favourably to this deal.
Ask that of me again, and you will find no more welcome among the harsh sands.
A negotiation must be handled like a writhing serpent. It might slip out of your hand... as it has done now.
The sun has set on our meeting, friend of Harad. We have not reached agreement here.
We can only hope that you asking this of us is a mistake.
Please, we know you to be different than the rest of the north. This offer is not agreeable.
Your long journey shall be rewarded with honesty. No, we can not accept this.
We enjoy your company. Please do not tarnish it by asking us to do what we can not.
I will pretend as though this was an offer mispoken. For your sake.
These halls smell. Shall I burn incense? No, it would be better to remove you and the stench of your lies.
Stare at the sun. Let it burn your eyes. Only then can you see the foolishness of your offer.
Even the flea-ridden beggars of Umbar's cisterns would refuse your terms. And you expected a lord of Harad to accept them?
This offer reminds me of you. Plain stupid.
Go back to whatever deep, dark, decrepid hole you came from and shove that offer back where it belongs.
We can not tell which is uglier. You, or this offer.
You ask too much. Give too little. We have no need of your kind.
If you think this has a happy ending, you haven't been paying attention.
Let the wind carry your offer away.
Your offer sits atop a hill too steep for us to climb.
The shamans guide us. They feel uneasy. We say no.
This is a bad deal. I do not agree.
The wild calls to us, and we must answer. Your path is not ours.
We can't. Please don't ask again.
A crow calls. Bad omens. We must say no to you.
I weep to reject a friend, but the elders say the hills rumble at these terms.
Your terms don’t sit right with the wilds. We must reject them.
Let our friendship hold, even if this deal does not. I must decline.
We remember your promises. Lies, all lies! We will not be fooled again.
We are not your dogs to be whistled for. Your breath is wasted here. Be gone.
I spit on you, this deal, and your grave!
Run. Hide. You will not escape the wilds.
I will shove your terms down your throat and use you as bait for my next hunt!
The shamans curse you. Our elders curse you. I curse you. The answer is no.

diplomacy_strings_string_offer_demand_de.value_original: The gathering storm threatens to engulf us all if we stand divided. Let us forge an alliance, a bulwark against the darkness, that our combined strength may yet win the day.
This is a great war long-planned, and we are but one piece in it. And now all realms shall be put to the test, to stand together, or fall under the Shadow,

Know that the blood of Númenor still flows strong within our veins, and we do not offer this alliance lightly. Yet, in the face of such peril, let us cast aside suspicion and forge a bond that shall endure.
diplomacy_strings_string_offer_demand_de.value_translated: Has de saber que la sagre de Númenor aún corre fuerte por nuestras venas, y que no ofrecemos esta alianza a la ligera. Aún así, ante tal adversidad, dejemos atrás la sospecha y forgemos un vínculo que nos fortalezca.

diplomacy_strings_string_offer_demand_de.value_original: Let us bind our fates together, as Elendil and Gil-galad of old. United, we may yet defy the Shadow.
Behold! The storm comes, and now all friends should gather together, lest each singly be destroyed. Let us league against the shadow, I beseech you!
The shadow lengthens, and the Dúnedain alone cannot stand against the tide. Let us join our strength, and together, we shall defy the encroaching night, and preserve what remains of this fair world.
Choose to stand with us now, or face the darkness alone. The White Tree will not come begging.
I hope to see in you a leader who understands the gravity of these times. An alliance, however tenuous, might be the shield that guards us all from utter ruin.
Let us speak plainly: the hour is late, and you can ill afford to stand alone. A union of our strengths, forged in mutual necessity, may prove to be your salvation.
Keep your bow ready to hand, and I will keep my axe loose in my belt.
Listen up, lad. A strong alliance, forged in iron and blood, is a hammer that can shatter any enemy.
We dwarves could show you a thing or two about warfare.
Us Dwarves can build more than halls y'know. We know how to make friends too.
You have my axe! Well, if you want it.
We've always been honest folk, honourin' oaths. Now we need yer honour, and yer strength, to survive. What say ye, lad?
So, here's how it's gonna be. We're offerin' ye a chance to prove yer worth. Stand with us, or get out of our sight.
This is no damn negotiation, lad. We're offerin' you a chance to save yer own worthless hides.
Yer tryin' me patience. Work with us and live, or stand alone and die.
An alliance with Rhûn is hard diplomatic currency, valuable, and difficult to secure. We recognize your kingdom's prestige in this offer.
The journey of a thousand miles begins with one step. Walk with us, and let us shield one another against all dangers.
Henceforth our valiant golden warriors stand in your defence, if but yours stand in defence of Rhûn.
We have been through much, you and I. Let us assure that should one of us be faced with strife, we combat it as one.
Dwarves, Elves, and Men amass in the West. A united force of our arms will hold them at bay.
Honor and glory heap on him who pledges his sword in defence of a friend.
Our dragon priests curse you, yet Rhûn cannot stand alone. Our enemies grow ever stronger. We must ask for your allegiance.
I detest even to utter this demand. Let us come to a peaceful accord. That is all.
All our enemies shall perish in the sun-fire of the East. Will you be one of them, or stand with the conquerors?

Do not think that merely by singing amid the trees, nor even by slender arrows from elven-bows alone, is this land maintained and defended against the Enemy forever. We would have your allegiance, if you would give it.
Le vaethor veleg. You are a folk of fierce warriors, but you too will be beset by the Enemy: this I foresee. It is your choice, then, whether you will stand alone, or fight alongside us.
Still we remember the waning of the Second Age, when Men, Elves and Dwarves stood together against the Shadow. Now is the hour to rekindle old bonds, to re-forge a union against the Dark Lord
Perhaps you never thought you'd die fighting side by side with an Elf. How about side by side with a friend?
The stars are veiled. Something stirs in the East; a sleepless malice. The Eye of the Enemy is moving. We must league against him, mellon, lest we shall fall alone.

I was there, three thousand years ago, when the Free Peoples united. I remember well the splendour of their banners, for it recalled to me the glory of the Elder Days. Let us now unite again, and banish the Shadow for ever.
The Valar weep at the very thought of an alliance with the servants of the Enemy, but I must present this treaty, for the hour is dire, and our light is waning.
Our paths have diverged in the past, to the sorrow of all. Let us not repeat the mistakes of bygone ages, but forge a bond that will withstand the trials ahead.
Do you not see? The Eye of the Enemy is moving. He is here. We stand against the encroaching darkness; will you stand with us, or fall beneath its wave?
Shall we make our counsels together against evil days, such that our estates shall both come to fairer flower than ever before?
A new Power is rising. Against it the old allies and policies will not avail us at all. This then is one choice before you, before us: We may join with that Power.
Surely you see, as a mind as astute as yours undoubtedly does, that the shadows lengthen, and no lesser power than Isengard can now offer stability and order.
Our friendship would profit us both alike. Much we could still accomplish together, to heal the disorders of the world.
The time of the Elves is over, but our time is at hand: the world of Men, which we must rule. I said we, for we it may be, if you will join with me.
A new Power is rising, and we must join with that power. It would be wise, my friend. Its victory is at hand; and there will be rich reward for those that aided it.
The kingdoms of old crumble, the Elves fade, the forests fall. A new age is at hand, an age of steel and fire, wherein your kind has no place. But take my hand now, and persist by my leave.
My patience for idle bystanders grows thin, as the gears turn ever onward. Would you be a gear that turns in unison with the machinery of progress, or be ground to dust beneath it?
There can be no victory against the new Power. Join with it, and be rewarded; or resist it, and be consumed. The White Hand offers no other choice.
If I am your salvation, you are mine.
The night grows dark, and full of terrors. Together, let us protect ourselves against them.
We shall perform in measure, time, and place if you would have us.
For behold the storm comes, and now all friends should gather together, lest each singly be destroyed.
The tides rise swift, and lone stones are soon drowned. Stand beside us and we’ll weather what comes.
They say the best defence is a good offense. They have never seen our spearwalls. Would you join the ranks?
Tighten your shield to ours, not from trust, but from dread of what follows if we fall divided.
The road behind is scorched. The road ahead is worse. But if we tread it side by side, just for now, there’s a chance we reach the end.
It's true we've clashed, but if we let the fire consume us now, there'll be no one left to remember why.
Thou art called to duty: serve in the defence of the borders of Mordor, unto thy death or the Master dismisses thee.
Cheer and applaud, for the armies of the Black Land deign to serve in thy wars, should thy land be attacked.
Sauron the Great has enemies in far away lands. He bids thee stand between them and and His realm.
Truly, Lugbúrz must have some favour for thee, for they offer to grant thy lands protection. I would accept this generous offer, lord, were I thee.
There is a mutual friendship between our two lands. I believe it is time that the benefits of such friendship be awarded.
The Great Eye bids thee to His defence. The foes of Mordor must never breach the Gate.
I do not understand it, but the Black Council demands an alliance with thee. I would spit on the parchment it is signed on, were thee any lesser of a lord.
My work is to deliver the messages sent out by Lugbúrz. This offer is clearly an error, but it is not my duty to correct it.
I have no belief that thy meager armies could defend the vastness of Mordor. Be grateful that thou hath the privilege.
My fighters will hold your enemies at bay, but I expect you to defend our warcamps while we're out fighting.
The West marches on us all. Stand with us and we'll hold them back.
Your walls and warriors won't hold forever. But we can help you hold a little longer.
You lot think you’re the biggest, baddest filth in the land? Maybe. But not invincible. We'll raise our shields for you if you do the same for us.
We fight together, we hold the ground, and we make sure no pinkskin sets foot where he don’t belong.
Well, you're not half useless after all. Best we cover each other’s backs before someone else puts blades in 'em.
Perhaps you want to be slaughtered. But if you want to survive, we'll help you. In return, you fight for us.
I'll send the snaga to defend your huts, but your fighters had better guard our border.
The Orcs will forestall your judgement, wretch, but you must keep the filth from our lands.
The great storm is coming, but the tide has turned. We can repel the enemy if we work together.
The only thing necessary for the triumph of evil is for good men to do nothing. If we stand in defence of one another, as good men, evil cannot triumph.
How shall any wall withstand such numbers and such reckless hate? We stand a better chance together than alone.
The enemies of Mordor must unite in common defence, for soon its scourge will descend on all lands, and none is stong enough alone.
Saruman is breeding an army in the caverns of Isengard to strike Rohan while Sauron attacks Gondor from the east. They are united in purpose, and we too must be... To stand against the coming tide.
Orcs are roaming freely across our land. Orcs bearing the white hand of Saruman. I bid you guard the borders of the Mark.
I never believed I would witness an Eorling siding with your kind, but the times are dire. Saruman defies Sauron, and thus perhaps there is strength even in standing with an enemy.
Rohan must survive this war, and if I am required to ask my enemy to raise his shield for me, I must do it.
Let it not be said that the Rohirrim are not warriors of honour and valour, for in this dark hour they would shield an enemy from his destruction. There may be no nobler sacrifice.
Let us shape the desert and jungle, to give life in times of the burning sun.
My scimitar is ready to defend you. But you must bind yourself to do the same to us.
Shoulder to shoulder. We stand against the tide. Will you join us?
We are friends in all but declaration. Let us remedy this position.
Together we rise from the sands, the waves, the jungles. United with the cause to repel those who underestimate us.
Let us announce to all who would hear that we stand as one.
A greater threat than you has come to our attention. We must set aside our troubles, for now.
This option is much better than me testing my scimitar on you, is it not?
The Lord of Mordor sees Harad as naught but a tool. No more! We make our own decisions. Stand with us, or fall.
Help us, and we'll help you. We can be strong together.
We want good warriors at our side. Are you a good warrior, or not?
The lone wolf dies, but the pack survives.
You are strong like an ox. Join us.
You trust us? Then prove it. Oath for oath. Shield for shield.
You have honour. Stand with those who have honour too.
You are weak. We are strong. You should follow our command.
Don’t like us? Don’t need to. Just link arms.
Stand next to us. Or we stand on your graves.

diplomacy_strings_string_offer_demand_pe.value_original: This conflict has grown wearisome, and serves only the will of the true Enemy. I extend an offer of cessation of hostilities, that we might find a path to lasting accord.
My ancestors, the Kings of Númenor, were mighty in war, though they were undone by their own pride. Let it not be so between us, and let us have peace.
For too long has the shadow of conflict fallen upon us all. I propose we lay down our arms, and seek instead a path where we might yet find common ground with you, for the sake of all Middle-earth.
Enough blood has been spilled between us. Let us speak of peace, that our strength may be turned against the darkness, not each other.
The blood spilled stains us all, and serves only the Enemy's purpose. I offer a hand in peace, not lightly given, but heavy with the hopes of a weary people.
The Eagles of Manwë weep for this conflict. Let us break this cycle of enmity and forge a lasting peace, a testament to reason instead of despair, though doubt gnaws at my spirit.
We have no love for your people, but we see the necessity for peace. Let us lay down our weapons, lest more destruction shall be wrought.
Consider this a last boon from the White Tower, offered in grim warning. Test our forbearance further, and our wrath will be unleashed, against which even the fire-mountain of Mordor seems milder.

Already the Anduin flows red with blood, yet still your banners are arrayed against our borders. We are weary of this foolish enmity, though doubt not that if it must be, we shall put even the last of your men to swift death.
By the beard of Durin, is there no sense in your heads? This war profits none, and ye better stop it sooner than later.
It's clear yer beatten. Pull back yer forces or we'll finish you off.
Imagine the coin we could make if not at war.
Good morning, my lads, enough bloodshed! Let's bury the hatchet, and forge a peace that lasts longer than a poorly-made axe head.
All this killing for what? When true enemies lurk in the dark?
Friends. We wish to share the ceremonies of feasts, not funerals.
I'm done wasting warriors on you scum. End this war.
Pretty simple choice, live or die, and I don't care which you pick.
Listen here, you lot. We're offering a truce, this one time. Break it, and be broken by our hammers.
Enough of my men have shed their blood in this war, and I will spare them if I can; yet they will not cease until my command is given.
Peace is an excellent thing, and war is a great misfortune.
To have peace there must be strife; both are part of the structure of the world. We have had strife. Will you have peace?
These battles are foolish. My men weep to cross blades with men they once called friends. Let us end this.
I wish to spill blood no more. It was a folly to sacrifice our friendship for petty ambitions.
In truth, I did not want this war. I cannot replace what has been lost, but shall endeavour to attone for it.
The thundering hooves will come crashing down upon you in the coming assault. This is your only chance to prevent it.
I have conquered lands that have no name in your tongue. If you wish to keep your own land, heed my words.
I would cease this bloody feud, if for the sake of my men alone. Will you spare your men, or would you widow every last of their wives?
The rivers of blood have flowed long enough, staining the very soil with sorrow. I offer you a chance to cleanse that stain, to seek a future where our children may walk in peace.
I have lived many ages in the West, and seen many defeats, and many fruitless victories. I grow weary of this futile conflict: let us now find accord, or else a swift ending.
Long strife has torn our kin apart, leaving a chasm too wide to leap over. Yet we offer now to build a bridge: cross it in good spirits, or find it crumbling beneath your feet.
Even Elven hearts grow weary of the shadow that lengthens; we desire no more the spilling of blood upon this ancient soil, only leave to shepherd what remains of beauty ere it wholly departs.
I seek an end to the bloodshed; a time to heal, if healing is yet possible.
My heart is heavy with the knowledge of what is lost, and what is yet to be. I offer a hand, though it trembles, in hope of a respite from the relentless strife.
The grace of Valinor bids me stay my hand, for now. Let not that be mistaken for weakness, lest your arrogance build you a funeral pyre.

Your assault upon the Eldar is like the play of a foolish child, thinking it may best its elders. But our patience wears thin: end this folly now, or learn why even Morgoth feared the wrath of the Firstborn.
What lies has the Enemy sown amongst your kin, that you make war upon us unjustly? Let us now rekindle the lights of peace, or find yours diminished forever.
Will you have peace with me, and all the aid that my knowledge, founded in long years, can bring?
Shall we have peace and friendship, you and I? It is ours to command.

Your sires have fought many wars, and assailed many who defied them. Yet with some they have afterwards made peace, none the worse for being politic. I say: shall we have peace and friendship, you and I?
Can we not take counsel together as we once did, my old friend? Can we not have peace, you and I?
I fear that in our past dealings, friend, I have lost patience, and indeed I regret it. For the common good I am willing to redress the past. Will you not consult with me?
Shall we not make our counsels together against evil days, and repair our injuries with such good will that our estates shall both come to fairer flower than ever before?
You have fought many wars and slain many men, and made peace afterwards. Can we not have peace?
Despite the injuries that have been done to me, in which your men, alas! have had some part, still I would save you, and deliver you from the ruin that draws nigh inevitably.
The Uruk-hai yearn for man's flesh, and it is only my hand that can stay them. Yield before me now, or argue with steel and blood.
I hate war as only a soldier who has lived it can, only as one who has seen its brutality, its futility, its stupidity. Let us end this war here today.
Unjust peace is better than the most just war. If you would have peace, I would have it.
We fight over an offense we did not give, with those who were not alive to be offended. Let us have peace.
Let’s not leave the memory of our dead with nothing but silence and suspicion. A treaty gives them meaning, and gives the living a way forward.
Peace, written and sworn, not to erase the pain of the past, but to end its grip on our future.
We never meant to raise blades in hatred. Only in fear, in duty. Let's end this war while we still call one another kin.
Let us remember that a traitor may betray himself and do good that he does not intend.
You can fight, in which case all of you will die. Or we can have peace, in which case only most of you will die.
Let this end, not for amity, but for necessity. Peace is the only coin left worth spending.
I almost pity thee. Thou would believe that any army could stand against the might of the Eye. Turn away now, in this rare moment of mercy.
Is not the suffering of thy people to be prevented? Take up no arms against Mordor hence, and they will be spared.
Let us remember Annatar, Lord of Gifts, and those He may bestow upon thee if thou would but stand down.
The Master grants thee a choice: back down now, or suffer His wrath. A lesser lord would not recieve such a chance, but there is worth in thee yet.
That we must wage war against one another is regrettable, and the Master would see it end.
My Master would see an end to the conflict between His forces and thine. Thou hath proven a worthy opponent, and so Mordor would have thee a worthy friend.
These are the terms: The rabble of thee and thy deluded allies shall withdraw at once, taking oaths never to assail Sauron the Great in arms, open or secret.
Our Lord Sauron the Great has no desire to pillage and burn all the world, He only demands servitude. This is thy last warning: cease resistance or fall.
Orcs gnash their teeth and scrape their blades along thy walls. Give up now, or thy life is forfeit.
You were neither friend nor foe before this bloody war. We’ll offer peace, but don’t give us reason to regret it.
Orcs know when a fight’s done. Stay out of our sight, and we’ll stay out of yours.
Live quiet under our shadow, and we won’t stomp your lands flat. Peace. That’s what you call it, right?
We fought you like enemies, but you're not strangers to us. The blood spilled, the losses...we know 'em same as you. This war ends here. You keep your side, we keep ours.
We were friends, but we crushed each other like sworn foes. That is war. But we'd set things right. Will you have peace?
No more blades. No more raids. We fought like enemies, but we weren’t. Not truly. We remember that. Maybe you do too.
We’ve bled enough, and so have you. We end this fight now, or we end you.
We end this fight now, or we rip through your ranks till there's nothing left but bones. Take the peace, or take the slaughter.
Lay down your arms, and keep your throats intact. Your choice. Our blades are sharp all the same.
No parent should have to bury a child, and yet this needless conflict claims many on both sides. Would you see the sons of your lands return home as we surely would?
I wish to build no more barrows for our Riders slain in battle. Would that you consent to end this war, that sons return home to their parents, fathers to their children.
The freothwebbe, peace-weavers, will do what is necessary for the survival of Rohan. Allow them to find husbands among your people, that this bloody war need not continue.
Enough blood has soaked the fields. Let us speak now, not of war, but of the quiet breathing of the land and the mending of what is broken between us.
My heart grieves for the fallen, both thine and mine. Let us not add more riders to the shadow-lands. I offer my hand in peace, though it be stained crimson.
Never before have I yielded to any man, ever since I could control hand and shield. Yet now is the time, for our true enemy lies elsewhere.
Your war-songs are faded, your banners tattered. We offer peace now, bought with the steel of our riders and the blood of your sons. Choose wisely, lest the dawn bring only your doom.
There is but one way to forestall your death. Declare an end to this war and your lives will be spared. Refuse, and be made a feast for the crows.
To offer peace when your death is within our grasp should reveal to you the honour and nobility of the Rohirrim. Your life, or your death, is in your choice today.
We live in a state of perpetual war, is it not time to bring some semblance of peace?
Crimson is not the natural way of the lands. Let us restore the safety in our peoples.
The braziers of war dim on this struggle.
There is no harmony in a war among friends.
Let us do away with this senseless feud so that our brothers may embark on more prosperous travels.
We come to you, horn in hand. A symbol of respect and peace. Will you take it and cease this war?
End this conflict before the full might of Harad bears down upon you!
You are not worthy of this peace we propose. Take it, before the wishes of the Black Serpent shift like the winds.
We call upon your shred of honour to end these battles. For a war will never be won against us.
The wolf that one hears is worse than the orc that one fears, and our wolves are at your doorstep. Only peace will sate their hunger.
The dark night has passed, and day has come again. But the day has brought strange tidings. Among them, this offer of peace.
The Moot has concluded. Peace is our path. Will you walk it with us?
You called us friend, even in war. If that’s true, mark it with oath.
You spoke fair as kin of the hills, even in war. Speak again, this time for peace.
We fought, but not as foes. Let’s make it right.
We’ve buried enough. Swear peace now, or dig your own graves.
Peace or blade? Choose.
The hills still echo with your war-cries. Make peace now, or hear ours next.

diplomacy_strings_string_offer_demand_tr.value_original: Our merchants bring the finest wares, crafted with the wisdom and artisanry of old Númenor. They are willing to trade at a fair value, if you consent.
We Dúnedain, facing ever eastward, have need of certain supplies. Therefore, I propose an accord between our peoples, a measured exchange that strengthens us both against the coming shadow.

Given the uncertainties that beset these latter days, it seems prudent to establish reliable avenues of commerce. A treaty of trade could prove mutually beneficial, affording you access to our craftsmanship and vital resources.
The craftsmanship of your kind and the wealth of your merchants are known far abroad. By virtue of friendship, will you not allow exchange of goods between our folk, that we both may prosper?
Though pride forbids me to plead unduly, the well-being of my people compels me. Consider the strength that a bond of trade might forge between us, against the perils of these darkening days.
Good friend, the shadow lengthens in the East. I would beg of you to consider a compact of trade between our peoples, a measure to strengthen us both against the encroaching darkness.
We offer trade not out of kindness, but necessity, so that your people may benefit as well as ours. Do not mistake this for weakness.

We seek no favours, only a just exchange to bolster our defences against a common foe. Let there be no illusions of goodwill; this is a pragmatic request, born of grim circumstance and steeped in caution.
Understand, we are not diminished, but necessity dictates certain measures. Present your wares, and we shall assess if they are worth the risk of us extending a hand.
Right, listen here. We need materials, ye need our craft. Let's cut the pleasantries and talk trade – if ye've the coin, that is.
It's the usual contract; summary of out-of-pocket expenses, time required, remuneration, funeral arrangements, so forth.
We heard yer coffers were thinning, and have the solution, but you'll need to pay up in return.
In days of old Moria and Eregion grew rich together. We'll do the same.
Friends, let's both turn a profit.
Gold. Gold beyond measure. Will you partake?
We've got the stones to trade with you filth. You in or out?
I'd sooner throw myself in a forge, but you need money, and we need money.
War ravages all. Do ye have the stomach to make up some losses?
Both your land and mine would surely benefit with exotic trade. Your peoples have goods I have never seen, and we can offer our culture's very best.
The clans of Rhûn have riches aplenty, more than what is needed to feed our own. Let us trade the excess, that we both may profit.
Should you desire our merchants carry your goods across the Sea to distant lands, you must allow them access to your markets.
Gold is the colour of the East! It stains our glass, coats our armor, and most importantly our coinpurses. Would you like some?
Though I am a mighty warlord, I too have the wit to run a kingdom. Gold from a friend is worth more than gold from bloody hands.
Let us grow rich together in trade. I have seen the fine wares of your markets and you have seen those of mine.
Your land has wares our Chieftains desire. It would be wise to allow us to buy them, before maps are unfurled.
Be grateful that we offer our wares to you. We would have conquered you already, were it not more expensive to do so.
We suggest trade only out of pity. We know that nowhere else your inferior wares would be accepted.
Long have we dwelt in twilight, ever watchful against the encroaching night; but even the Eldar find need of commerce, and we would fain establish a bond of trade with your folk.
Behold! These fine wares are of ancient Elven-craft, even recalling the splendour of lost Doriath. Would you withhold them from your people, or shall we trade and prosper?
Our silver-ware shines bright, mirroring the light of Eärendil's star. We give it to you in trade that shall enrich both our realms and illuminate our future.
As the Shadow lengthens, the need for allies who trade in more than just words becomes ever dire. Let us establish a bond, woven with shared prosperity.
The flow of goods between our peoples would be as a river nourishing two lands, a testament to alliance in these waning days.
My coffers hold riches born of ancient trees and starlight, things that might well ease burdens, and you possess crafts equally rare. Bangathab, let us trade, for it avails us both.
We have observed your people's works. In exchange for certain crafted goods, we may deign to share the bounty of our forests, though our generosity should not be mistaken for weakness.
The artisanry of the Eldar surpasses yours in skill, and is not easily bartered. Prove that you possess more than mere shiny objects, and we might be willing to consider an exchange.
We are not blind to your need, and willing to exchange goods. However, understand that Silvan-cut gems are of far greater worth than whatever baubles you possess.
The Uruk-hai have had enough maggotty bread. Give them some meat.
The storehouse of Orthanc grows thin. Re-supply it, that you may have the counsel and friendship of the White Wizard.
The army of the Uruk-hai must be armed and fed. Aid me in this endeavor.
Surely, my friend, you would not hem the river of trade that might flow between us, nourishing both our realms?
The forest of Fangorn lies on my border. It shall be ripped down to fuel the fire. What have you to offer in exchange for some of this timber?
Word of the famed delicacies and precious trinkets that your kin make has reached even my ears. They deserve a place in my personal stores.
Isengard has need for slaves, for the Uruk-hai take no captives. Let us strike a trade-deal, lest I have to take them by force.
Alas, ere the age of industry takes hold, Isengard needs to procure lesser wares in a conventional way. Thus, you are to deliver your goods, for a minor compensation.
Do not assume that I think your wares valueable. Nay, Isengard merely needs fuel for the furnaces and crude iron for the smelters.
What we lack, you hold in plenty. What you seek, we can provide.
Let us open our roads and our storehouses to one another, that no shadow may find root between us.
We seek fair exchange. Let us open trade, and perhaps understanding will follow.
Friendship, like the hearth, must be fed to keep its flame. Let us strike a trade.
Let trade be the bridge between our halls, lord.
Friendship alone does not fill the granary. Let us make it fruitful and have trade.
Trade with us, and you may find fewer reasons to guard your borders.
Your granaries thin. Trade with us, or test your pride against hunger.
Trade could ease your burden. Or shall we see how long your war effort lasts without salt, iron, or grain?
If thy merchants can survive the long journey to the East beyond our mountain borders, we would have them bring their finery to Mordor.
We found many relics when the Gondorians abandoned their watch in Mordor. We have no need of them, but they should fetch a decent price for thee. In return, we expect something of value to us.
The prison Thaurband houses many of Mordor's slaves. Shouldst thou require labour, we will trade them with thee. But, I cannot guarantee they will survive the journey to thy lands.
The great forges of Durthang work night and day to produce weapons and armour for the host of Mordor. If thou wouldst have some trade for a measure, show us what thou hath on offer.
Orc draught sustains the armies of the Eye on their long marches. For thee, it'll be an aquired taste. I have plenty of barrels ready to trade.
Contrary to Gondorian opinion, Mordor is not all desolate. The fertile farmlands of Núrn produce our crops. Let us trade.
diplomacy_strings_string_offer_demand_tr.value_translated: Contrariamente a la opinión gondoriana, Mordor no está completamente desolado. Las fértiles tierras de Núrn producen nuestro grano. Vamos a comerciar.

diplomacy_strings_string_offer_demand_tr.value_original: What would thou offer us? Thine eyes? Thine ears? Thy tongues? Thy very lives... in return for petty trinkets, for that is all they are worth.
A market is a rare thing in Mordor, and thy wares would be rarer still. Perhaps in Seregost I would offer them.
I would have thy metals, with which we would forge into swords to dismember thee with, ha!
Your lands are fat with things we want. Give us meat and steel, and you get a few bits of treasure.
You got food. We got blades. Let’s trade.
We offer trade. You accept, you live fat.
The fires of our war machine must be stoked, same as yours. Let us trade and fuel the fires.
We need what you got. You need what we got. That’s called trade. Don't be stubborn.
You give us meat, coin, slaves, and we'll forge your weapons and armour. Crude, but effective.
Listen up! We want your goods, and we'll have them one way or another. I'd much rather knife you, but we've got other plans...
Consider yourself lucky that we'd trade with you at all. With the spoils of our wars we could buy your whole kingdom.
Trade now, and we might not remind your people how loud they scream.
Rohan's woodcarvers, smiths, weavers, masons, clamour for the opportunity to see their products sold in distant lands. We would likewise welcome yours in the Mark.
Finer steeds you find nowhere in this Middle Earth. Should you trade with us, you will have them.
The wide green pastures of the Wold provide more than enough for the sustenance of our people. Let there be trade between us, so that the excess goes not to waste.
Hail, and may your fields be ever green! Rohan has much to offer, and we would share our bounty with you through a fair trade, for the good of both our peoples.
There is much exchange to be had between our lands. Advise your merchants to turn west as they leave Anorien to the north, for that is a safer road to Edoras than by the Old Pukel Gap.
There ought to be trade between our lands as we are friends in all things. We are eager to welcome your merchants to our markets and pray ours are welcome in yours.
There is a route that passes through the East Emnet. Your merchants should travel that way on their journey to the Wold. Pay the roaming warg-packs no heed.
We will not use your crude iron armor or swords, but would purchase them from you. Perhaps they can be melted down and reforged into horseshoes.

You have shown me none but trinkets that clutter a home and collect dust. Nothing of any use or value to us. If you wish the merchants of Rohan to sell your goods, you must be willing to compensate us.
Word of our caravan masters express new opportunities in these lands.
He who controls the spice controls Middle-earth.
The winds of trade blow to your lands.
You've slept on our rugs before. Now, you may share them among your people. For a price.
An exchange of wares so that your people may lavish in the wealth of Harad.
A peaceful greeting to you. Harad has wares, if you have coin.
Deals behind closed doors mark the difference between a chief and the Black Serpent.
Our goods fetch high prices in your black markets. We know this, because your goods do the same in ours. Let us negotiate a deal.
Smuggling is in our nature. We can work something out.
We hunt the wilds for meat and furs. We can trade them to you, for a price.
You have things we lack. We have that which you desire. Let us speak plainly of trade.
Though our town markets are modest, we are not without skill in craft. And we know trade.
Our bellies grow thin. Let us trade, that our children may eat.
We ask for little, only what helps us both. Share your bounty, and we'll share ours.
My people offer what we can. Take it, and give us what we need to survive.
You don’t like us. We don’t like you. But trade fills bellies. Let’s deal.
You call us savages. Yet your stores run dry. Let’s see who needs who.
Trade with us, or guard your roads better.

diplomacy_strings_string_offer_join_war_.value_original: Your foe is ours also. We would lend you the strength of the Men of the West, if you would have us by your side.
It is not fitting that your good folk should suffer alone while our brave men stand idle. Tell us your need, and we shall march against your foe.
The enemy you face is but a tendril of the greater Darkness. We offer our banners to stand with you, that we united may hold back the night.
Certainty of death? Small chance of success? What are we waitin' for?
Hmph, heard ye got a proper fight brewin' with them skulkin' dogs. Where do we sign up to bloody their lands?
My axe is restless in my hand. Give me a row of orc-necks and room to swing and all weariness will fall from me!
The warlords are preparing for battle. They know there is great glory to be gained in your wars. Let us come with you.
We have seen your honour in battle, and we would match it. Speak the word, and we will sally out with you.
Should you ask it, the golden dragon will take flight to your aid. Our warriors beyond number will march beside you.
You have my bow. I beng nîn linna ar i vagol lîn: may it sing with your sword, and bring swift death to your enemies.
Our bow-strings are drawn, and eager to release swift arrows upon these foes of Elvenesse. Gurth ani chyth wîn!
The world is changing, and we are not heedless of what troubles befall mortal lands. Let us aid you, that the Light of the Eldar shall purge the darkness from your lands.
Are you in need of assistance? You have spent much of your power. Leave your enemy to me.
My fighting Uruk-hai want man-flesh to eat. Give them leave to conquer, and your enemies will tremble before you.
The walls of your enemy, you see, would be most useful for testing new machines of war I have devised. Let me unleash the devilry of Orthanc upon them.
Let us join your cause, and in victory, let us share in the spoils.
I do not know what effect my men will have on your enemies, but they terrify me.
It is better to be the right hand of doom than in its path. My forces would march with you.
Sauron the Great deigns thee worthy of His aid. The host of Mordor will cover thy enemies like a great flood.
The gaze of the Great Eye is fixed upon thee for a time. The forces of Mordor would join thee in battle.
Our Lord Sauron does not seek to undo this world, but rather to reshape it. He would begin with the lands of thy enemies, for they are ours as well.
The Dark Lord calls. We answer. We’ll tear the guts from His foes. No mercy. Just blood and ruin.
Let us loose on your enemy. We get restless when we stay in camp too long.
We'll bring slaughter and fear to your enemies. When the dust settles, only Orcs will be left standing.
We will come, if you wish our aid. Ten thousand spears I shall send over the plain to the dismay of your foes.
We may yet be avenged. Let us gird ourselves and weep no more! Come! We have a long road, and much to do.
You have formidable infantry, lord, but your armies lack in cavalry. Let the Riders of Rohan march with you to battle and victory is assured.
Every time we come you inquire about the Mûmakil. Now, you can fight alongside them.
War is the birthright for many young Haradrim. Would you deny them?
Let us join you, to rid these lands of cowards!
The young warriors long for blood. Let us have that of your enemy.
I am a warrior. I fight where I please, and I win where I fight. Point me to your enemy.
Look, you've got an enemy. I only need to know one thing: where they are.

diplomacy_strings_string_offer_single_pa.value_original: Perchance this subsidy from the Dúnedain might be of timely assistance. Accept gold as a token of our friendship and support for your worthy efforts.
These are dark times indeed, and friendship is more precious than gold. Still we would offer this boon, a measure of relief against the encroaching darkness.
Consider this payment as a testament to our mutual benefit, strengthening the bulwark against the peril that looms over all free peoples.
We extend our coffers as a token of good faith.
We have no more room in our vaults. Take this.
Spend coin to make coin.
Great fortune befalls you today, my friend. Our chieftains are pleased with your works and your deeds, and would express this pleasure with gold.
Your name is upon the lips of the members of the Golden Court. They would see your power and wealth grow.
Know that I could well build golden statues proclaiming the glory of the valiant instead, yet I offer you this gift. Be grateful today.

The Valar lament the sorrows of Middle-earth, and though we are sundered from their blessed shores, our hearts are not deaf to your woes. We offer this payment as a glimmer of hope against shadows that threaten to consume all.
Mabo hen. Take this boon from the Eldar, sent in these days of twilight, that you may yet preserve what is fair and good in your lands.
May this gift be a light for you in dark places, when all other lights go out.
While I have long cast off base desires, I understand that a gift of gold may yet sway mortal men, or sweeten a deal that appears too brash.
I am not blind to the uses of gold given freely. May this grease the gears of diplomacy; let good-will reign where common sense lacks support.
I presume you require a certain incentive to wholly embrace the way of progress. Perhaps this modest subsidy proves sufficient.
Gold speaks where words may fail. Take this coin, and know that we are not without means, or intent.
This is not a gift, but an investment. Coin now, cooperation later.
Let this payment open doors that words alone cannot.
Whether for some pity or some true value that He finds in thee, the Master has deigned to give thee payment. Thou wouldst do well to remember this, lord.
This coin was forged in the very chasm the Master wrought His Ring. It is a great honour to receive it.
Orcs do not have wits to make use of gold. Take this so we can be rid of it. We should rather forge steel, not coin.
No tricks, no traps. Just a chest full of shiny things you’ll never find on your own.
The Orcs would see you prosper, if but to be an appealing target for our raids.
Here, take this, swiftly. Don't tell the others I'm feelin' generous today, or they'll all come creepin'...
We have horses to spare and gold enough, thanks be to the bounty of the fields. Let this payment ease the burdens of your people, and remind you that Rohan remembers its friends.
The miners have struck a new vein in the Glittering Caves of the Hornburg. We would share some of this newfound wealth with you.
diplomacy_strings_string_offer_single_pa.value_translated: Los mineros han dado con una nueva veta en las Cavernas Centelleantes de Cuernavilla. Estaríamos encantados de compartir parte de este afortunado descubrimiento con vosotros.

diplomacy_strings_string_offer_single_pa.value_original: We descendants of the Éothéod are a proud people, yet generous to those we deem worthy of friendship. We proudly present you this token.
Take these wares. Our bazaars are overstocked.
Our people offer a boon. Will you have it in rugs, incense or cloves?
It is tradition that when the desert gives, we give back. Do not disrespect our ways.
The hunters have done well this season. Take this gift of their bounty.
We pay you now. You remember it later.
This is a gift. Perhaps repay it with kindness.

diplomacy_strings_string_personality_des.value_original: The bulwark of the free peoples of Middle-Earth against those who seek domination and destruction, Gondor harbours a deep hatred for orcs, but remains on good terms with elves and other men.\\n\\n[[col:green]]- Moderate diplomatic bonus with Elves and Men[[/col]]\\n[[col:red]]- Major diplomatic penalty with Orcs[[/col]]\\n[[col:red]]- Severe relations penalties with followers of the Power of Shadow.[[/col]]
diplomacy_strings_string_personality_des.value_translated: Siendo el baluarte de los pueblos libres de la Tierra Media contra aquellos que buscan dominación y destrucción, Gondor alberga un profundo odio hacia los orcos, pero mantiene buenas relaciones con los elfos y otros hombres.\\n\\n[[col:green]]- Bonificación diplomática moderada con los elfos y los hombres[[/col]]\\n[[col:red]]- Gran penalización diplomática con los orcos[[/col]]\\n[[col:red]]- Severas penalizaciones en las relaciones con los seguidores del Poder de la Sombra.[[/col]]

diplomacy_strings_string_personality_des.value_original: Strives for supremacy over its neighbours in the east.\\n\\n[[col:red]]- Moderate diplomatic penalty with other Easterling factions[[/col]]
diplomacy_strings_string_personality_des.value_translated: Se esfuerza por la supremacía sobre sus vecinos en el este.\\n\\n[[col:red]]- Penalización diplomática moderada con otras facciones de los orientales[[/col]]

diplomacy_strings_string_personality_des.value_original: Harbours a deep envy and disdain for Rohan, but feels neither animosity nor goodwill towards most of its other neighbours.\\n\\n[[col:red]]- Major diplomatic penalty with Rohan[[/col]]
diplomacy_strings_string_personality_des.value_translated: Alberga una profunda envidia y desprecio por Rohan, pero no siente ni animosidad ni buena voluntad hacia la mayoría de sus otros vecinos.\\n\\n[[col:red]]- Gran penalización diplomática con Rohan[[/col]]

diplomacy_strings_string_personality_des.value_original: Harbours a profound hatred for orcs, but is either on friendly terms or indifferent towards its other neighbours.\\n\\n[[col:green]]- Moderate diplomatic bonus with Dwarves and Men[[/col]]\\n[[col:red]]- Major diplomatic penalty with orc factions[[/col]]\\n[[col:red]]- Severe relations penalties with followers of the Power of Shadow.[[/col]]
diplomacy_strings_string_personality_des.value_translated: Alberga un profundo odio hacia los orcos, pero mantiene relaciones amistosas o indiferentes con sus otros vecinos.\\n\\n[[col:green]]- Bonificación diplomática moderada con los enanos y los hombres[[/col]]\\n[[col:red]]- Gran penalización diplomática con las facciones de orcos[[/col]]\\n[[col:red]]- Severas penalizaciones en las relaciones con los seguidores del Poder de la Sombra.[[/col]]

diplomacy_strings_string_personality_des.value_original: On good terms with other Free Peoples and have excellent ties with Gondor; but their hate for orcs runs deep.\\n\\n[[col:green]]- Moderate diplomatic bonus with Free Peoples and Dúnedain factions[[/col]]\\n[[col:red]]- Major diplomatic penalty with Orcs[[/col]]\\n[[col:red]]- Severe relations penalties with followers of the Power of Shadow.[[/col]]
diplomacy_strings_string_personality_des.value_translated: En buenos términos con otros pueblos libres y con excelentes lazos con Gondor; pero su odio por los orcos es profundo.\\n\\n[[col:green]]- Bonificación diplomática moderada con las facciones de los pueblos libres y los dúnedain[[/col]]\\n[[col:red]]- Gran penalización diplomática con los orcos[[/col]]\\n[[col:red]]- Severas penalizaciones en las relaciones con los seguidores del Poder de la Sombra.[[/col]]

diplomacy_strings_string_personality_des.value_original: Strives for supremacy in the vast deserts of Haradwaith.\\n\\n[[col:red]]- Major diplomatic penalty with other Southron factions[[/col]]
diplomacy_strings_string_personality_des.value_translated: Se esfuerza por la supremacía en los vastos desiertos de Haradwaith.\\n\\n[[col:red]]- Gran penalización diplomática con otras facciones sudronas[[/col]]

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_dunedai.value_original: We wish for no strangers in the land at this time, unless they be mighty men of arms in whose faith and help we can trust.
An hour is all that I have to spare, for there is much else to heed. Much of more import, it may seem, and yet to me less pressing.
Though the Stones be lost, they say, still the lords of Gondor have keener sight than lesser men, and many messages come to them. Sit now, and tell me your tale!
We grant you audience. Speak, and let your words be weighed with care, for in these uncertain times, trust is a coin not lightly spent.
Let your embassy be brief and to the point, as befits the gravity of this hour. We attend your message.
Well met! We offer you such courtesy as we still have to give, but time is precious, and sorrows weigh heavily in these days.
Be welcome in these halls, friend of the West, where you may yet find refuge from the shadow.
Come, kindred spirit! Let us speak as allies, like Elendil and Gil-galad of yore.
Your arrival is ever timely. What news and counsel do you bring from your noble people?
Enter, friend, and be welcome. Here the light of the West yet burns, and those who uphold it find the doors of the White Tower ever open.
Greetings, friend of the Dúnedain. Rest from your journey, and let your words be heard with honour and goodwill.
Many dubious vagabonds are wandering the roads as of late, yet in you we find a welcome visitor. For your arrival brings a spark of hope in these shadowed times.
Do not think that I shall easily be deceived! The eyes of the White Tower see far, and much that is not said may well be guessed.
Keep your forked tongue behind your teeth! I have not come to bandy crooked words with a witless worm!
Perhaps we should cast you into the Anduin, to see if your hollow words keep you afloat!
Is it not the custom for ambassadors to use less insolence? Unless your master has come to new wisdom, then with all his servants you will be in great peril.
So you expect me to listen to your treacherous appeals, as Ar-Pharazôn heeded the Deceiver? Nay, I have more mastery of lore than you presume!
The errand-boy of a faithless lord, I presume? Speak what you are commanded, though I doubt much wisdom will issue forth.

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_dwarves.value_original: There must be a reason why yer here.
Well, stranger, what do you bring from your lands? News? Or, better... salted pork?
Hm? Wasn't expecting to see ye here.
Traveled all this way, have ye? Got somethin' on yer mind?
Aye, come in, come in. What's on your mind, then? I'm listenin'.
Speak yer piece, then. I haven't got all day for idle chatter.
By my beard, yer shorter and wider than last we met! Now, fill up that mug!
Aye, laddie, you have come just in time for the salted pork! Let's show you some Dwarven hospitality!
You have shown your usual cunning in getting up just in time for a meal.
Come for some fabled Dwarven hospitality, eh?
I'll ne'er turn down an ale with a friend.
Hmph, speak your mind, friend. No need to stand about like a lost goblin in the deeps.
Ishkhaqwi ai durugnul! I spit upon your grave!
Bah! A cave-troll is a more welcome sight than you, and the better negotiator!
Bring up the strong ale! I can't stand this fool while I'm sober!
By Durin, not you again! Go kiss a goblin's backside if you've nothin' better to do!
Ye beardless elf huggin' oathbreaker. What do you want?
Bugger off, or talk to my axe-head!

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_easterl.value_original: Truth is the foundation of all enduring things. Speak in truth, as I will do the same.
Beware of releasing the restraints in you, listen if you want to endure in the mouth of the hearers. Speak after you have mastered the craft.
Another guest in my palace. I trust your words shall not betray you. I am listening.
I will treat with you if your words bear truth. If they bear honied lies, you will never leave this place.
Choose your words carefully. In Rhûn, everyone, even a king, is held accountable for the sounds of his voice.
You seek audience with a Chieftain of Rhûn. You have it, but know that you will be watched closely.
Honoured guest, how may I be of service?
My palace is a place of truth and repect. You honour me with your words, and I shall honour you.
You are welcomed to the Chieftain's palace, friend. Speak and be recognized.
It is wise that you would seek me out. We value you, for you have done us well before. How can I be of service?
My palace is open to you, noble one. Partake in my hospitality, and then we shall speak with earnest tongues.
You have journied far, friend. Come, let us speak about what needs to be said.
Your traditions are insane, and your language is babble. Speak quickly, for this court is a place of honour.
I grow tired of you and your attempts to sway me. What are your words this time?
Away with you! It is not the time for desparate pleas and empty promises. Speak only if you must.
There were two, Allatar and Pallando, who sought audience as you do now. Woe unto you if your words are but an echo.
I will listen to your words. Then, I will decide whether to have my guards cut out your tongue.
The flowery tongue of Elves falls on deaf ears here. Speak words we understand, then be gone.

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_elves_0.value_original: Hither you have journeyed, and for this we bid you welcome, though shadows lengthen across even this realm.
We Elves seldom give unguarded advice, for advice is a dangerous gift, even from the wise to the wise, and all courses may run ill.
Welcome, wanderer. The light of the stars guides your feet to my dwelling; speak now, what burden or joy compels your presence?
The fading light graces your presence. What matter of import draws you to this realm, so that you seek out my counsel?
Unburden your heart and speak your piece freely, for within these halls, counsel and consideration are ever offered.
Your arrival is not unwelcome, though certainly a matter of import must have moved you to find our guarded realm. Unfold your proposal, then, for I am eager to listen.

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_elves_f.value_original: Mae govannen! A star shines on the hour of our meeting.
Be welcome! You appear kingly, even as the lords of the people of Fingolfin; I would that I had a brother so valiant.
Le suilannon! Let us sit beneath the stars, and take counsel together.
I mâr nîn i mâr lîn. Ever you are welcome in these ancient glades, elf-friend.
I sense a purpose woven into your footsteps. Unfold your thoughts, and I shall listen with patience.
The river of time flows ceaselessly, yet here, within these borders, we may share a moment of respite. Tell me, what purpose has brought you to this sanctuary?

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_elves_h.value_original: Doubtless you came in haste to this table, and may be excused your ragged cloak; but there is no need to leave your head untended like a thicket of branches.
You bring graver news to me than seemed likely. Take heed now to all that you say; for this is a court of doom.
Daro! Go no further, herald of darkness. Your very presence sullies these fair woods.
You bring great evil with you. Go no further!
No dhínen, pen-channas! Do not trouble me with your witless speech.
I have little time for idle chatter with lesser folk, for the long years have stretched my patience thin.

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_isengar.value_original: Let us understand one another, and dismiss from thought the lesser folk!
Speak, then. I trust your errand is of sufficient import to warrant disrupting my contemplations.
Greetings. You sought my presence, and now you have it. Speak freely; I have little patience for hesitation.
Welcome, welcome. I trust your journey was not unduly hampered by the wilderness? The age of untamed nature will soon yield to the order of efficient design.
Ah, so the moth flutters to the flame. Speak, little petitioner, and try to articulate your purpose with more clarity than a hobbit explaining the proper timing of meals.
It has seldom been heard of that you sought for aid, one so cunning and so wise, wandering about the lands, and concerning yourself in every business, whether it belongs to you or not.
You are declared by your noble devices, and still more by the fair countenance of your house. Let me be of aid to you!
Smoke rises from the Mountain of Doom. The hour grows late, and you ride to Isengard seeking my counsel. For that is why you have come, is it not, my old friend?
Enter freely and share your purpose, friend. I am always receptive to reason, and perhaps I can illuminate the path before you with my wisdom.
Ah, welcome, friend. I perceive in you a mind keen to understand the turning of the age; approach, and let us speak of the possibilities that lie ahead.
I bid you welcome, wise one. It is good to see that not all are blind to the necessity of change; come, and let us speak of how we may bring order to a new age.
Welcome. Your arrival is timely. A new power is rising, and I suspect your capabilities may be of use in the forging of an age of order.
Why must you disturb my rest? Will you give me no peace at all by night or day?
What is your house but a thatched barn where brigands drink in the reek, and their brats roll on the floor among the dogs? What is it you want now?
If you wish to treat with me, while you have a chance, go away, and come back when you are sober!
Your presence here amuses me. Tell me, how long do you believe your antiquated ways can withstand the forging of a new age?
Well? Have you not been gifted with the power of speech, or has fear stolen your tongue now that you stand before true power?
One would hope that your audacity in seeking me out is matched by the worth of your words. I sincerely doubt it, of course.

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_middle_.value_original: I will aid you, or I will oppose you. My choice depends on your words and deeds.
You are under my countenance. My word is on you. Let us speak.
You’ve come far, and we’ll hear what you have to say.
I don't like you, but Orcs I hate more. What do you need?
The world turns, and strangers meet. Let us determine our parts to play, for good or for ill.
I receive you in good order, as courtesy demands. What you bring to this table, we shall weigh with care.
Ah, a welcome sight! Our hearths burn brighter when friends cross the threshold.
You are honoured in these halls, for you are ever a friend of my people. Come and sit, and let us talk.
We receive you with respect and regard. For much may be gained when friends meet in good faith.
Your arrival brings hope for what lies ahead. Let us speak plainly and with purpose, for there is work worth doing together.
You are welcome in these halls. I have awaited your arrival with baited breath.
If you come to me claiming you mean well, then I'm a hobbit.
Upon the next tree you shall hang alive if your words are false.
Yes, we are interrogating some of your warriors in the next room. Speak loudly so I can hear you.
You are received, but you are not welcome. Speak.
You risk much coming here. Choose your words well, for the ground beneath you is thin.
Say what you came to say, but know this, not all wounds are healed by word.

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_mordor_.value_original: If thou wouldst speak with me, it would suit thee to bend thy knee, lest I cleave it from thy torso.
My Master, Sauron the Great, bids thee welcome. Is there any amongst ye with authority to treat with me?
So thou wouldst speak with me. Of what worth are thee to the Eye?
Thou wouldst make a bargain with the Eye. A wise choice, for Sauron the Great demands allegiance from all who walk this Middle-earth.
There is a wild look in thy eyes, as though thou hath crossed paths with one of the Nine. One becomes accustomed eventually.
In these halls, it is expected that guests bow to the lords of the Tower. I expect no less from thee.
The Eye speaks highly of thee, lord. How may I be of service?
Always a pleasure, lord. Let us hope that Lugbúrz finds thy worth as high as I do.
Thou art well known in the Black Land. I need not remind thee of the benefits and consequences of such reputation.
I welcome thee to my hall. The atmosphere is welcoming and warm, is it not?
Thou hath chosen wisely in seeking counsel with me. There exists no mightier force in all of Arda than the will of Sauron the Great.
Welcome, lord. I hope the orc rabble outside did not dirty thy robes.
Bow, wretch, before those who bear the Eye.
We grow wary of thy inane babble. State thy wishes and deliver me from thy presence.
Hast thou seen the new slave-camps down in Thaurband? I hope they accommodate thy people well, ha!
Thou hath erred, thrall, to find thy way to me. For thou wouldst find belonging only in the slave-mines, amongst thy enslaved folk!
Declare thy purpose, insignificant one. I await thy paltry offering.
Thou hath crawled far to fall at my feet. That alone is worth my attention. Let us see if thou art able to keep it.

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_orcs_01.value_original: Life in the warcamp is cold, dark, brutish, and short. Say what you will, while you still have the time.

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_orcs_02.value_original: You are neither dead nor dying. What is your purpose here?

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_orcs_03.value_original: You are not an Orc, uruk, or goblin-man. Why have you come to our camp? Speak quickly.

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_orcs_04.value_original: You’ve either brave or foolish to come here. Speak, and let's find out which.

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_orcs_05.value_original: Come, talk, we'll see what your mouth's worth. Our ears, and knives, are sharp.

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_orcs_06.value_original: Not many walk through our gates and still have shadows. What do you want?

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_orcs_fr.value_original: Ah, another warchief. How fare your warriors? Hopefully you brought some man-filth entrails.
Servant of the Eye be welcome to my warcamp! Do you bring word from the Master?
diplomacy_strings_string_receive_orcs_fr.value_translated: ¡Siervo del Ojo, bienvenido a mi campamento de guerra! ¿Traes noticias del Maestro?

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_orcs_fr.value_original: Speak quick, friend of the fanged. You come unbloodied, and that buys you our patience.
Well now, look who rides into my warcamp. Been a long time, my blood-brother.
Bold of you come in person. We like that. Sit, share meat and draught, talk war.
We set no traps today. You've earned that much. Now speak.

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_orcs_ho.value_original: You've got until I finish my draught. Get to rambling. When I'm done, I'll decide if I gut you.
Skah! What dung pit did you crawl out of?
Hmm, what about your legs? You don't need those, do you? I've had nothing but maggoty bread for three stinkin' days!
What kind of pinkskin crawls into his own grave in search of hope?
Well, well. The sheep walks into the wolves’ den.
Words before war, is it? Fine. Spit your talk. We’ll nod like it matters…

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_rohirri.value_original: This is the realm of the Rohirrim, and none ride here save by leave of the King. Who are you? What is your haste?
Guests are not allowed in the Golden Hall of Meduseld so armed. Leave your weapons with my guards, and let us sit by the hearth and talk.
In the morning counsels are best. Then you shall look on the muster of Rohan and ride away the gladder for the sight.
I do welcome you, though I admit the courtesy of my halls could be found lessened of late.
The road is perilous, and few travel here without cause. If your errand is of weight, speak plainly, and we shall see what may be done.
The winds carry many tidings in these days of war. Tell me, what brings you to Edoras?
Bring wine and food and seats for the guests! At the table, some men may do the greater deeds, we say.
Hail, valiant king! For such one are you. What words would you speak to me this day?
Let the horns sound your arrival, lord. The Golden Hall is prepared to receive you as honoured guest.
Though the days grow dark in Rohan, you shall e'er be welcomed here my friend.
Rohan keeps faith with its friends. If you have come seeking aid, say what troubles you, and let us find strength together.
Long may our peoples' bond endure. You are welcome in my hall as kin, not merely as my guest.
Late is the hour at which you choose to appear. Láthspell I name you, Ill-news, and ill news is an ill guest they say.
Here you come again, and with you come evils worse than before, as might be expected. Why should I welcome you?
I greet you, and maybe you look for welcome. But truth to tell your welcome is doubtful here. You have ever been a herald of woe.
Leave your weapons at the gate, and do not expect courtesy in these halls. I will not suffer you for long.
You would approach, yet the blood of my people stains the land by your hand. Speak swiftly, if you would have words instead of steel.
Rohan does not treat lightly with those who have sought its ruin. Say what you will, but do not think me so easily deceived.

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_southro.value_original: You have travelled far indeed to reach my lands. I trust that you have important business?
Harad welcomes you. Let us speak, but be warned, I grow weary of serpent-tongues.
You are strong indeed to have braved the desert and arrived in my halls. That alone gives you more worth than most.
A journey well traveled is currency enough for parlay in these lands.
Tell us, what news do you bring from the north?
All agreements begin the same: With a welcome. So, we welcome you.
I look forward to your journeys, my friend. I am glad to see you here as my guest once more.
Dawiker! The desert has been kind to you. Let us reflect on its temper and speak together.
Sit, rest a moment! The journey here must have been exciting, was it not? We will talk later, tell me now of your travels.
You are strong indeed to have braved the desert and arrived in my halls.
The carpets are comfortable, my friend. Sit a while, we will smoke and eat before the sun sets. Then we will barter.
Oh my! How fortuitous of you to join us. Reminds me of the first time I found an oasis...
The sands should have buried you alive, kiztis! Why do you stand before me?
Dawiler, fiend within these halls. I will not welcome you, but it is my duty to speak with you.
Today we may speak of the jewels of the South, but it would take much convincing to let you leave these halls with anything but sand in your boots.
We are men of the sands, the seas, and the sun. You are men of weakness, cowardice, and villainy. Get your business over with.
Your presence is nothing short of peeling a sunburn from ones skin. Do us the favour of keeping your petty requests short.
Our people have weathered storms far more mighty than you. What burden do you bother our people with today?

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_wildmen.value_original: You have traveled far. What do you seek among the forgotten?
Wisdom is welcome here, wherever it comes from.
You've interrupted the hunt! What do you want? Don't waste my time, for I could just as easy hunt you.
You come to the men of the wild. The hills may flower, but may be full of serpents. We're listening.
You can not tame the wilds. Remember this as you speak.
We have empty cages. Speak badly. You fill them.
You come as friend? Then speak. My ears are open.
The hills welcome you. Will you sit and feast? With full bellies then we shall talk of diplomacy.
Greetings, friend of the tribes. Let us show you hospitality.
Welcome to the hills. The fire is warm, sit with us.
diplomacy_strings_string_receive_wildmen.value_translated: Bienvenido a las colinas. El fuego es cálido, siéntate con nosotros.

diplomacy_strings_string_receive_wildmen.value_original: Speak, and be heard. The hills welcome your voice, friend.
Finally. A head I don't want to sever.
So, the dogs have found their way to my door. What whining do you bring, strawhead?
The fool is busy in everyone’s business but his own. What foolish words have you come to bring?
Let's play a game. Which body part do you need the least? If you do not want to play, be gone.
You think I'm some sort of savage? You're right. But Ghân-buri-Ghân would cut out your tongue and feed it to you, rather than listen.
The shamans gave warning of your arrival. You carry lies and darkness.
Rats hide from danger. You run towards it. Perhaps you are stupid.

diplomacy_strings_string_reject_demand_j.value_original: Alas, we cannot spare any men for your war; for we are beset on many borders, and must look to our own defence first.
Noble as your plea is, the line of Númenor bears a heavier burden than you know. We can offer no assistance at this time.
We thank you for your consideration, but the safety of our people is paramount. We must stand alone, as ever, against our own enemies.
The Dúnedain are not some ragged band of mercenaries, to be deployed at your every wish!
Do you truly believe we are fools, to throw ourselves into a conflict not of our making? Whilst we hold at bay the shadow, what battles have you fought, save those for petty claims and borders?
So, you believe our valiant men some lackeys to be summoned at your whim? I suggest you learn to defend your own borders.
The world is grey, the mountains old, the forge’s fire is ashen-cold; No harp is wrung, no hammer falls: The darkness dwells in Durin’s halls.
So, you think a few sweet words and a fancy hat will sway us? This war is yours, and yours alone to suffer through.
Ye will not have my axe today.
Stone and steel, lad, we're not mercenaries to be hired! Take your pitiful request elsewhere, before I lose my temper.
You dare ask the sons of Durin to fight your battles? Go back to your masters, tell them we're busy mining our own business.
No 'mount of coin would move me to form a shield wall alongside ye.
The clans will not unite for some petty grievance. Perhaps some foolish warlord out there will aid you, but not this day.
I have not commanded that we march, and so we will not march.
The blood of the clansmen is worth more than the gold lining the Sun: no drop will fall without price.
Who are you, one who should dictate our ibasti? The chieftains would have your head for this arrogance!
Did I hear you right? You would command the hosts to war? Ha! Go away, little lord.
Our Chieftains struggle to unite the clans to battle, and you think you could do it yourself. I envy your audacity.
We lament the troubles that beset your realm, but the fate of mortal men lies beyond the bounds of our weaving. Our kin have long chosen to stand apart, and we shall not forsake that path now.

You think of yourself and your own glory, and bid us each do likewise. But we must think of others besides ourselves, for not all can fight and fall, and those we must keep from war and ruin, while we can.
The part of my people in the war I rule according to my own wisdom. No force of arms I will send out at this time; nor at any time that I can yet foresee.
Think you the Sindar some band of mercenaries that go hither and thither to their master's bidding? Nay, our forest will not suffer the stain of your insolence.
We have watched empires rise and crumble into dust. What makes you think your petty conflicts hold any significance that warrants the shedding of Elven blood?
We have fought many wars upon Middle-earth, yet none for causes so base as yours! Perhaps an extended visit of our dungeons can purge these insolent thoughts from your mind!
