I will tell you where your doom will be decided. The path that you are set on can only lead to death, and I shall not join your fate.
I am occupied with matters of greater consequence, and meddle not in the squabbling of lesser kingdoms.
I did not breed the fighting Uruk-hai just for them to be used as some mercenary force for irrelevant conflicts. They will be deployed only at my command.
Against the power of Mordor there can be no victory.
Aid you? Nay, you are doomed to fall, and so it is just. For the weak must make way for the strong, as the old age makes way for a new one.
Your pleas fall on deaf ears. If you were devoid of foresight to enter a conflict with no chance of victory, then at least face your doom with courage.
I do not slay man or beast needlessly, and not gladly even when it is needed.
You will need more than one companion in your dangerous adventure. Speak again once you have found some.
We have no quarrel in your war, and no cause to shed blood for it.
We fight for our own, not for those who eye us with contempt.
We see the trap behind your call to arms. We will not march at your side, nor under your shadow.
You raise steel against us, then ask us to fight at your side? We are not so broken as to serve those who would see us fall.
We would not go to war today, for if we did, we'd have to march all day.
Only the Lord of the Black Tower can command the armies of Mordor to march. Find some other army to die for thee.
Thou art not His Grace, Lord Sauron the Greatest and most Formidable; as such, thy command hath no weight in these lands.
Fall upon thy own sword and feel the sting of the cold blade, lest I do it to thee myself! What a maddened request!
Thuo art weak, begging and pleading for the strength of the Master. He will never grant it to thee.
Thy actions have earned thee scorn in Lugbúrz. They would not commit even the lowest snaga to thy cause.
Ha. Tryin' to drag us into your mess. Your wars ain’t worth the rust on our blades.
The Orcs will not be fodder to fight in your wars. I wouldn't even give you the snaga rabble.
Hmm, you don't look like the Great Eye. I think my warriors will stay in camp.
We's sooner gouge out our own eyes than fight alongside you.
We ain't dying for your quarrels. You want blood spilled? Try your own first.
Our wars are bloody and cruel. Yours are squabbles for fools in shiny boots. You don't know what war is.
Why should Rohan ride to the aid of those who did not come to ours?
You may march to war, but not to your victory. Even with our forces, we would be outnumbered. I will not sacrifice the Riders of Rohan needlessly.
Our people are safe, but we have paid for it with many lives. The eorlingas will not ride to war with you this day.
Your master calls for aid? Rohan lends steel to honour, not whim. Return and tell him the Rohirrim serve no errand boys.
The Rohirrim will never ride to war beside you! We will not dishonour the victorious dead with such fell deeds.
That an enemy of the Rohirrim would bid us to war alongside him is a tale such as I have never yet heard. Surely you understand this is impossible.
We don't care to kill them. They are not worthy of our blades.
Some borders even the Haradrim cannot move. Very few, but you're on the wrong side of the fight to move them.
War for the sake of war divides the clans. The Black Serpent declines your demand for battle.
We will not fight your battles for you, so you can stab our backs later.
You would have the beastmasters ride our Mûmakil into battle alongside you? I would rather see them loosed against you!
And you believed that we would not only stand aside, but shed our own blood for your gains?
Our axes are not yours to wield. We owe you nothing.
No. We are not mercenaries.
Fight your war yourself. Or are you too weak? Grow stronger, and leave us out of it.
Do you think we're fools? We see only desperation in your eyes, not honour. Keep your war to yourself.
You want our blades? Take them...point first.
Fight for you? We’d rather feed your bones to the crows.

diplomacy_strings_string_reject_demand_s.value_original: Our own needs are pressing, and we offer no succour at this time.
With due respect, your claim, while perhaps justified in its own right, cannot be accommodated at this time.

Understand, if you will, the White Tower demands constant vigilance, and each silver piece must be weighed against the looming darkness. I am afraid that we cannot honour your demand for recompense at this time.
Those who stretch out their corrupt fingers to reach into our treasury may well find them hewn off!
You mistake our grace for weakness, knave. Return from whence you came, and spread the word: the blood of Númenor shall not be bought, nor its coffers plundered by such dogs.
You think the treasurer of Gondor some merchant to be bargained with? Take your demands elsewhere, lest I silence your impudence another way, one far less to your liking.
We will not open the vaults to you.
Coin is king. We will not be dethroned.
I will not part with a single coin. Not one piece of it.
Payment? From me? You’ll get naught but a swift kick down the mountain for that kind of insolence!
What do you take me for? An elf?
You want our gold? We can give you an axe instead!
The streets of Rhûn's cities are lined in gold, but that gold was not won without blood.
This gold is for the peoples of Rhûn, as is their right. Go and make your own coin with your crude smithies.
You ask coin from the golden dragon? He is more likely to turn your kingdom to naught but ash.
Ha! You wish for a tithing? Seek some other naïve lord.
If gold is what you want, then gold you will have. Would you like it coating your burning skin or poured down your throat?
I did not attain such great fortune by throwing coins at beggars like you.

The wealth of the Eldar lies not in mithril or jewels, but in the preservation of beauty. Take not coin, but instead what wisdom you find within these glades, if you would seek it; for that is freely given.
The wealth of the Eldar is not measured in trinkets nor yielded by threats. We offer friendship and counsel, not tribute to passing shadows.
Though our halls are open to those who seek wisdom or aid, they are not storehouses to be plundered by those who mistake kindness for weakness. We owe you nothing.
By what right do you presume to demand recompense from the Eldar? The light of Valinor shines far from your grasping reach; take heed lest its fading memory burn you.
Why, 'tis but a little boon for a stranger to ask. Nay, even if you brought before me a Silmaril, I would not grant your desire.
Your audacity is a bitter draught to swallow. My patience is already strained thin as moonlight on water. Return from whence you came, ere it finally breaks.
Assume not that I am devoid of gold to fulfill this contract. Quite the contrary, this proposal is devoid of reason. What you offer in return is barely worth such a sum.
Perhaps your scales, friend, are not well-calibrated. Do you not see that your demands far outweigh the benefits of this arrangement?
The treasury of Isengard is not some merchant's ledger to be opened at will; indeed, far greater matters now demand my financial attention.
By what right do you demand tribute from Saruman of Many Colours? Nay, even the Dark Lord would not dare such insolence. Know your place, little one.
A trifling sum, you say? I deal with knowledge, power and the forging of a new age, not with haggling merchants. Begone, mewling whelp, for your babbling exhausts me.
Ever you speak of payment and compensation, yet offer naught of worth in return. Come back when you have gained a semblance of political competence.
We owe you no debt, and we do not pay without cause. Seek your coin elsewhere.
The middle-men are beholden to none. We will not pay what is not owed.
Our treasury door is closed to you. If this is a test of our resolve, you have your answer. We will not pay.
You want our gold? Take it. We'll see how that ends for you.
No coin will leave our coffers for the likes of you.
You’ll find no gold here. Only men ready to die before they yield.
Beggars and peasants, always demanding gold from my purse. Go away!
My Master does not give gifts to any but His most trusted servants. Thou art not considered to be of such worth.
Oh, I did not think that thy kind could comprehend currency. No matter, I was not prepared to give thee gold anyways.
I own a knife of very fine and ornate craft, imbued with gold and laid with gems found only beneath the Ephel Dúath. Thou may have it, but only thrust in thy bodice!
I have heard that in some Rhûnic lands, they pour molten gold into the throats of traitors. Maybe it would suit a beggar better...
There is a chasm outside, a deep one, where thou might find some gold bits. I encourage thee to leap into it.
Sure, we’ll pay. One sack of dung, one sack of teeth. All freshly taken.
We don't pay strangers, we bury them. You pick which.
You got guts, I'll give you that. But Orcs don't pay tribute. Leave now, befor you don't got guts anymore.
You want tribute? Come take it. Let’s see how much your corpse can carry.
We owe you nothing but pain. Enemy hands don’t get paid. They get cut off!
You come to my warcamp with empty chests expecting payment? We'll fill them. With your eyes, ears, and tongues.
We must spend our coin in our defence, as the White Wizard would see Rohan fall. We cannot spare it even for you.
Alas, the treasure-vault of the Hornburg is emptied, and Rohan possesses no coin for you this day.
The Rohirrim are a frugal people. I speak plainly to you... you will not have our coin.
Begone, craven. The wind from the Mark carries no coin for dogs that bark loudest.
He that would see the Mark in ruin, burned, shall not be provided means to make it so.
Reach for our coin again, and return to your land with your begging hand hewn off.
It is rare to see rain in the desert. As it is rare to see Harad deliver charity to the weak.
Our treasury is as a scorpion of gems. Fair to behold, but reach for it, and you will be stung.
Harad's wealth serves no obligation to fill your purse.
You command us to fund your war-path against Harad?
We will never sharpen your blades with our coin.
Thievery in plain daylight is no bolder than this demand!
We will offer hospitality if you seek rest, but not payment. Our treasures are not yours to claim.
I owe you nothing!
We give nothing to those who give nothing back.
Your kind have grown fat on lies. We will not feed your greed today.
We pay in steel and blood, not silver. Choose your next words wisely.
The last one to ask for tribute from us is buried in the hills. Do you intend to join him?
We have pondered this request, but deem the risk too great. These are not the times to open your borders for foreign men.
It is not our custom, nor is it prudent in these times, to grant passage to armed companies through our lands. Therefore, your request cannot be granted.
The defence of the realm requires that all paths be kept secure and under our sole command. We must decline, so as not to compromise this vital necessity.
Though I wish it were otherwise, I must refuse. The fief-lords would not take kindly to the presence of foreign hosts, be they friend or foe.

My Lord, whilst we appreciate your aims, the roads are perilous enough for our own folk in these darkening years. To permit passage to others, however well-intentioned, risks drawing further shadows upon lands already beleaguered.

Do not think that we mistrust your men or your good intentions, but the burdens upon our people are already too heavy. We must keep close watch on our borders, and cannot permit any armed men to pass.
So, you presume me a dotard, who has grown blind to your purposes? We will not open the gates for vagabonds who would abuse our hospitality!
A bold request indeed, when the Enemy watches our every move. One might wonder at the true purpose behind such a movement so close to our heartland. Nay, I shall not be deceived so easily!
Of what use are city-gates, if left open to all? I do not extend this courtesy rashly. Keep your forces to your own lands; we trust only the blades sworn to the defence of this realm.
I understand yer need, but granting passage? It's out of the question.
Go around the mountain, not through it.
We can not allow the danger of your soldiers roaming our lands while other pressing matters echo through the mansions.
We fear the grumbling is too much to allow yer troops through our lands.
Yer allowed here as friend, not as a soldier.
Please honour us by keepin' your wars out of our montains.
Over my dead body will your soldiers march through these halls. Get out, before I introduce you to the pointy end of my axe!
Are you daft, lad? Not a chance. Turn back now before I lose my temper.
To freely march yer soldiers upon our mountains would be to sign the funeral tablets.
I cannot trust your men to leave our lands unscathed. We honour the steppe and the forest alike, and would not see them tainted.
Your men will not be safe here, and we will not be safe so long as they remain. Do not expect this to change.
The great lands of Rhûn are wide, but there is no room for you.
I cannot allow you to pass this time, honoured guest.
We honour you in battle and in counsel, but we cannot honour your armies upon our soil.
Though we may be friends, the lands of Rhûn have never known loyalty from anywhere but within. The clans would not suffer foreign blades in our towns.
Your men carry crooked blades and more crooked faces. They will never enter Rhûn with open arms.
If you cut even a branch out of my forests, I shall cut your head off!
I suppose next I will hand you a Chieftain's golden helm, and have all our men lay down their arms? Begone, churl.
The rivers of my realm do not flow towards war, and neither shall its paths become paved with the march of armies not our own.
The forest-paths have not been trodden by strangers for ages, and shall not been opened now.
I have given this request consideration. However, it would be unjust to my people and to our forest to allow armed passage so hastily.
While the plight of your people is understood, my heart cannot turn against the safety of my own. To grant passage is to invite the storm into the boughs of our ancient trees.
Alas, the forest-roads have grown dark and dangerous, and our March-wardens have been hard pressed to keep vigil. We cannot further endanger our realm by letting anyone walk there at will.
Understand that it has ever been our custom to keep close guard around the forest, such that none may enter save at the King's own will. We do not now abandon this lightly, even for a friend.
These are our ancient and well-guarded glades, not some worn country road to be trodden upon with iron-clad boots!
It is not without reason that any vagabonds are shot at sight on our borders. We do not suffer brigands to scourge our forest, nor spies to bring tidings to the Enemy.
We have not suffered trespasses in more peaceful times; now the Enemy stirs, and you think we would let ruffians wander about at will? Your insolence is an insult against our ancient wisdom!
The roads of Isengard are not intended for frolicking dalliers to have their afternoon stroll. The fighting Uruk-hai march on them, and will not suffer any hindrance.
The lands of Isengard are not, as they once were, but homely gardens and quaint greenery. I entertain visitors no longer.
The Gap of Rohan is closed to vagabonds, marauders and mischief-makers. I see no need to grant you passage.
Most esteemed friend, while your purpose is certainly noble, I fear the passage of armies would prove disruptive to my rather delicate ongoing experiments.
I sympathise with your urgency, old friend, and fain would like to grant you passage. Alas, the roads of Isengard are over-full already, as timber and steel must be steadily supplied.

Entertaining visitors is one thing, my friend, but having steel-clad hordes of soldiers wear out my roads and bridges? I trust you understand that it would only be just to demand a fitting compensation.
Yea, and I shall also offer my high chamber in Orthanc for you to dwell in, and my personal stores for your sustenance? Begone!
Your request is as absurd as it is audacious. Tell me, why should I extend hospitality to those who give me brag and abuse?
Ah, yes, why should you not freely enter Isengard? I so enjoy dallying truants wandering my porch, and spies creeping into my weapon-stores.
Our lands remain closed to foreign arms. Such presence would stir unrest we cannot afford.
The Middle-men guard their borders as they guard their word, with care and resolve. We cannot let your armies pass.
I see no gain in granting you passage, but much risk. The answer is no.
We cannot grant passage to any host, no matter how trusted.
We cannot allow foreign troops to cross our soil. Our people would not understand
Our lands are not a thoroughfare for war. Let friendship stand without the tread of your boots upon our soil.
We know the weight of your boots and the shadow they cast. You will not march through our lands. Not now, not ever.
You’ve given us no reason to trust your march, and every reason to bar it. You will not cross our borders.
We know what follows in the wake of your armies. We will not let that shadow fall on our soil.
I cannot fathom any reason that thou would want to traverse our lands. Nor can I fathom a reason to allow thee.
Even if we did grant thee passage, there are foul beasts in these lands that would kill thy men.
I assure thee this: any shortcut through Mordor will hinder thee far more than the long path around it.
Thy men would succumb to the poisonous fumes of Mordor. Our orcs can withstand it. The Great Eye would not have thee waste their lives.
If thou must reach some foreign land across our border, I would suggest finding a new route. Only the Master's armies may traverse.
There is no reason for thy men to hide away in dark corners of our lands.
The bravest and most durable of thy men would surely die a horrible death, should they rest but one night in Mordor. Stay away.
There are mountains around Mordor for a reason! We do not want you lot here.
I am almost tempted to let thee: the thought of orc bands slaughtering thy hosts at night amuses me.
If I'd let anyone walk up to me, I would've been knifed in the dark already.
You walk our roads, you walk into spears. Best stay where you’re welcome.
Asking to march through... so you map out our warcamps... sounds like spy-talk.
Mordor's Orcs march around the Dead Marshes to get to the Gate. March around our lands. It's the same idea.
These lands are ours. You step in, you step wrong. Even friends get lost in the dark.
Our roads ain’t yours to march. A friend knows better than to stomp through our lands.
Military access? Hah! You want a tour too? Maybe a map and a snack? Get lost.
Meat-lumps don't get passage. Unless you want to walk right up to the campfire, and get roasted on the spit, ha!
You want to march through our lands? Try it. We’ll pave the road with your bones.
Neither elves, men, nor dwarves have business in the Riddermark. Your are not to enter these lands.
If you enter these lands, the enemy will surely come and attack you here. And if you are forced to retreat, the shame and reproach will be great. So do not enter them.
No army has ever breached the Deeping Wall. I would have it no army ever breach the border of Rohan.
Even though your host be friendly, it marches towards doom, and I will not risk open war in Rohan. Your armies must pass outside the borders of the Mark.
Isengard has loosed the Uruk-hai and Dunland wildmen upon the Mark. It is not safe for your army to travel here.
I will not have the green fields of the Riddermark stained red as the presence of your armies cause the enemy to attack. You must go around Rohan's pastures.
Should Rohan allow you passage, just to let the Westfold be pillaged by your marauders? Nay, your forces are forbidden here.
Should I grant your army leave to march to Edoras and burn the Golden Hall of Meduseld? No, I think not. Enter my lands and you shall surely perish.
There is a pile of burnt Uruk-hai carcasses rotting near Fangorn. This is our warning...do not cross the boundary of Rohan.
The sands of Harad are a wild and unforgiving place. You would not bode well here, and so you will not.
I think it best you do not travel here, lest you find yourself a "guest" at a Troll-man's feast...
The tales of the treachery of these lands are false. In fact, the truth is much worse than our folklore. Do not come here.
These lands will kill you, friend. And we do not have enough scouts to spare.
We deny you passage on this day. It is for your own good.
We have jungles, if you did not know. Tales are not shared of them, for men do not return once ventured there.
Oh? Shall we open our gates as well? Allow your troops to garrison the sands?
Never, ever, shall we allow snow-eaters passage into these lands.
Why do you even ask? You know we will say no, and you will march your troops against the desert either way.
Your war is not our war. Keep your armies far from our valleys.
Last time soldiers passed through, the trees still haven’t grown back.
Your men would not be safe in the wilds. Wolves, wargs, and darker things prowl.
My people are as the wolves. Your men are not safe here.
Friendship with us is one thing. Marching through our hills is another.
Friendship ends where war-paths begin. Stay on your side.
This is our home, not your road to somewhere else. Go back where you came from.
You'd set fire to our hills as you march through them. We know better.
You’re not passing through. You’re not passing at all.

diplomacy_strings_string_reject_demand_v.value_original: The White Tree stands tall and shall not bend to such a wind. Your claim of suzerainty is rejected; we shall govern our own affairs, as we have for centuries past.
Know this: Gondor bows to none, least of all to thee. Thy proposition is an insult to the White Tower, a wound to the memory of Númenor itself.
We have stood against the Shadow for ages uncounted. We require no overlord, and we shall remain free, or fall fighting to the last man.
The heirs of Númenor kneel to no foreign lord! Your demand is an impertinence we shall not suffer, for we are a free people under our own ancient rule.
You think the blood of Númenor runs so thin in my veins that I would surrender this realm, defended by countless generations, to your petty ambition? Begone, you and your insolent demands!
diplomacy_strings_string_reject_demand_v.value_translated: ¿Pensáis que la sangre de Númenor corre tan débil por mis venas que abandonaría este reino, defendido por incontables generaciones, a vuestra vaga ambición? ¡Marchaos, vosotros y vuestras insolentes demandas!

diplomacy_strings_string_reject_demand_v.value_original: So, you come before me and presume to speak of vassalage? Nay, the Dúnedain bow to no upstart kingling, nor yield their ancient freedom to any who crawl from the shadow.
The Dwarves have no need of your protection. We'll fight to the last.
I've heard some daft things in my time, but that takes the biscuit. We will never be your vassals, so save your breath and get out. Now!
Dwarves are too proud to bend to a foreign ruler. We stand firm.
By Aulë's beard, you expect us to serve you? Bah.
Never! Speak such insult again and you'll leave a head shorter than you came!
I don't think ye want to know my answer to such offense.
The clans do not know your name and many do not even know your lands. They would laugh to hear your demands.
Tell to your master that my power has reached beyond even his dreams. Now, remove yourself!
Resilience is the mark of true strength. Rhûn shows true strength this day.
You would subjugate us? Insane fool! One hundred clans and tribes make up our might!
Have you no mind to the power of Rhûn? We conquer and subjugate those around us, not the other way around.
Rhûn does not bow to those demanding the knee. Only when every warlord lies dead will we consider your words.
Oaths the Eldar swear to no-one; this have we learned harshly, and we well remember the Kinslayings. And least we would swear to you: for who are you to claim overlordship over the Firstborn?
Our king is the Elder King who dwells upon Taniquetil, and we are pledged only to preserve what still is fair upon Middle-earth. You cannot have our fealty.
You think the light of the Eldar diminished far indeed, to make such a proposition. Nay, ere the last of our strength fades, we shall not suffer to be held unfree in the Hither Lands.
Have you ingested an orc-draught, perhaps, that has poisoned your mind and tongue? You are but a maggot, writhing in the filth of your own corruption. Be gone, or be slain!
Fealty we swear to no one, and no king we suffer above us but Manwë Súlimo, the Elder King. Remove yourself, lest the wrath of the Eldar be upon you!
Do you forget to whom you speak? You are no lord of Men, and least one of Elves. No more are you than an escaped thrall, and your master's chain still awaits you!
Saruman the White Wizard, Saurman Ring-maker, Saruman of Many Colours, bows before none. Isengard will not serve thee.
Do you suppose the Tower of Orthanc at your command? By what power of the One do you hold sway over me?
You would gaze upon the Palantir of Orthanc as if you were its keeper. You will never be, as I will never yield to you.
You dare to demand obedience from Saruman of Many Colours, mightiest of the Istari? You and whose army?
Now that you have finished your jest, let me turn to lighter matters: to devise, say, a fitting reward for your hindrance and insolence.
You misunderstand power, o pitiful creature. The future belongs to the strong and disciplined, while you offer only weakness. I will not suffer any further insults.
If this is the price of your favour, then we must do without it. We will not be vassals.
The middle-men are not your subjects to command. We do not bend the knee.
We may not be mighty, but we are free. That freedom is not yours to claim.
We will not kneel. Try to force us, and you’ll find we still have teeth.
You’ve given us little cause for trust, and less for loyalty.
Press us further, and you may find resistance where you expected submission.
The Kingdom of Mordor and it's subjects serve none but the Eye. I cannot imagine that it would ever subject itself to thy will.
Little lord, doth thou not know? Speaking and demanding conquer no kingdoms: it is only through great bloodshed.
I have little belief that thou could rule the petty slave lords in Núrn, let alone all of Mordor.
The land of Mordor...serve...thee? Ha. When I'm done tearing thee apart, there shall be gore enough to wrench the most savage of orcs.
And thou art...? Ah, I had forgotten that thy kingdom existed.
Get thee gone, and come back never again. I am assured now: thou art mad.
A quick way to get knifed if I bend the knee to you.
Nice words. Polite threats. But we ain’t fooled. Orc warchiefs do not bow.
What kind of warchief would I be if I submit to you? I know, a dead one. The others would see to that.
Bow to you? Bah. We eat things taller than you for breakfast!
Slaughtering all those men of yours has made kneeling a bit difficult. I think we'll stand.
Vassals? Is that your fancy word for slaves? Get out of here before you lose your head.
Such words are ill-spoken in the Golden Hall. Rohan has never bent the knee, and will not now.
The Riders of Rohan answer to no master but their own. Begone, and speak no more of such folly!
We are a land of horse-lords, not vassals, and our loyalty is to our own hearth and home.
Your words are poison, and your demands an insult to the Rohirrim. Take them back to the shadow from whence you crawled!
We are no dogs to lick your boots clean, nor thralls to bend knee to your arrogance. Leave this land, or be borne out upon the tip of my spear!
Your offer is a jest, a fly buzzing around the ear of a war-horse. We choose death before dishonour. Now begone!
You could not domesticate the sands even if you wanted to. They deserve to be free.
From where we hail, we execute merchants for offering deals as horrid as this.
Ha! And we thought you'd travel all this way for real business.
We'd sooner raft through the bay of Belfalas, paddle-less, than bend the knee to you.
Ask this question to one of our Mûmakil. They will offer a more accurate answer than I.
The only time we bend the knee is to set up rug in the tents!
Wildmen are wild, free, but not children. We will not be lorded over as an adult does a child.
You want a vassal? Find weaker folk. The wilds stand free.
Our fathers knelt to no one. We will not kneel now.
We bend to no one. Our fathers bled on this soil. We will do the same before kneeling to the likes of you.
You would burn our land. Now you want our oath? Die wanting.
You're no lord of the hills. Never were. Never will be.

diplomacy_strings_string_reject_offer_de.value_original: You stand on your own, and there is nothing more that I can do to help it. The board is set, and the pieces are moving.
Your intentions, you say, are noble. Yet Gondor has stood watch against the Shadow for an age, and we find our own strength adequate for the tasks that lie ahead, for the moment.
Such pledges are readily spoken, but rarely endure the test of battle, particularly against foes of such vast malice. We maintain our own vigil, and wish you fortune in your own strife.
This offer is generous and not without wisdom, but we must stand alone in this hour.
My lord, your offer is weighty indeed, and laid before us with a sincerity that I do not doubt. Alas, our needs are pressing, and we cannot afford entanglements into new alliances.

The blood of Númenor is not easily swayed, and although I am tempted by the promise of unity against the Shadow, I must heed the council of my advisors. The cost is too high, the risks too great for our weakened realm.
You speak of aid and succour, yet your cringing demeanor belies your true intent. We will not be chained by bonds forged of false promises!
Do you take me for some gullible churl, that I would yoke the fate of Gondor to your ramshackle cause? I find myself wondering if you are a tool of the Enemy sent to mock us.
You imagine we, descended from the Kings of Númenor, would stoop to grasp at straws proffered by your people? One must presume that the fumes spewn forth from Orodruin have clouded your judgement.
Aye, I hear your offer, but we'll stand alone, thank you very much.
We appreciate the thought, but our axes are sharp enough. We'll handle our own troubles, and you handle yours.
No. We don't need your kind interferin' in our affairs.
Durin's folk must weather the storm like te rock and stone we are. We will not look to our friends to shield us.
Don't mistake our refusal for disrespect, friend. We just can't. Our hands are tied tighter than a goblin's purse strings.
The risk is too great for our people. Best of luck to ye, friend.
I have seen how you treat your friends. When they came to you starving, homeless, seeking your help. You turned your back
Hah! An alliance? You insult me, you insult my ancestors, you insult every dwarf that ever swung a hammer! Away with you!
A pile of coin the weight of my beard couldn't make me say yes to form a shield wall alongside you!
If a warrior cannot face his enemy alone, then he is no warrior, and deserves his fate.
You have come seeking our aid, yet what you offer we do not require. Our golden warriors defend themselves. You will not dishonour them.
Our dragon priests curse your foes, but Rhûn will not spend the blood of its warriors in your defence.
You have mighty enemies, honoured friend. The clans are not prepared to be called to your side.
I cannot accept, for we have our own troubles to deal with. Perhaps when the hordes are assembled we will be ready, but not today.
I have little love for your land, though I have respect for your people. We will not lay down our lives for you.
No true warrior of the East would defend the likes of you.
Your men bathe in rivers and eat at the same table as your peasants. They will not defend us, nor will we them.
I would never offer you my blade by your side, but you can have it through your heart!
The fates of Firstborn and Aftercomers may be entwined at times, but must at last find a different end. We are loath to forge bonds that would not last forever.
We thank you for seeking common cause, but the long memory of Elves sees perils you may not yet perceive. We are wary of entangling our fate with yours.
You speak hastily of bonds and fellowship, but we have stood alone for ages, an island amidst shadow where the glory of the Elder Days may yet be preserved.
Your hand is offered in fellowship, a generous gesture indeed. But our watch is a solitary one, as it has been since the days of yore, and we must decline.
Sometimes two streams may run alongside one another, and yet never converge. We cannot forge lasting bonds, for I foresee that the currents of fate carry us apart.
The years lengthen in the Hither Lands, and the light of the Eldar fades. We shall not abide here for ever, but at last depart to the West. The coming age is yours, and you have to stand alone.
You speak of alliance, yet we perceive the truth: that you would plant a sapling of poisonous weeds in our fair forest, and sow discord amongst our kind.
Too long have I walked the Hither Lands and clashed with the Enemy, that I should now not discern his lies seeping through your speech. Leave, servant of shadow!

You speak of friendship and succour, just as Sauron treated with Celebrimbor. Unlike the kin of Fëanor, I am not ambitious nor easily deceived; but you shall find my temper likewise fiery, if you persist!
The age of antiquated oaths and alliances is over. Isengard needs no pacts nor treaties that bind its power, nor sycophants hiding behind its might.
Things are swiftly at motion, and a new power is rising. The bonds of oaths and fellowship would be but a burden now.
I trust you understand my hesitation, for the times are uncertain, and even the wise cannot see all ends. I would not forge bonds today that might be cast off tomorrow.
My friend, a formal alliance would, forsooth, be well and just, but alas! There are promises already made, plans already forged and forces already set into motion. Would that you had asked sooner!
Your people, who have ever been friends and allies of Isengard, are undoubtedly stout-hearted and brave, but I fear my fighting Uruk-hai will not be so... welcoming.
Your borders are strong and your warriors well-renowned, would you not agree? I trust, then, that you will be capable of standing by yourself.
I know not why I have had the patience to speak to you. I need you not, nor your little band of gallopers, as swift to fly as to advance.
So, the meek and lowly seek shelter behind the walls of the powerful, as is their wont. I have no pity to spare for your kind, nor shelter to give for those unworthy of power.
Ha, an alliance, you say! I need not even a glimpse of the Palantir to see your intentions, your war-mongering and malcontent. But worry not, you shall find war soon enough.
We shall not raise sword nor shield at the call of another, lest our own hearths be left unguarded.
We shall not bind ourselves to a storm we do not yet understand.
We are not yet tempered for such a bond.
To bind ourselves in defence, even with a trusted friend, is to wager our safety on the fortunes of war not yet ours.
We cannot make your cause our own. A shield raised for another may leave our own flanks bare.
Our hearts are with you, but we are not prepared to make our shields yours.
If you fear attack, see to your own walls. We will not be your shield.
The middlemen will not bleed for those that seek their downfall. Guard your own gates.
You ask us to stand guard beside you, though we have long stood guard against you. Curious.
Sauron, Lord of the Earth, has no need for an ally now. His armies stand ready to cover the world in Shadow.
Do not presuppose the host of Mordor requires thee to defend our flanks. The breeding pits ever produce new orcs to serve and die for the Master.
Barad-dûr is nigh impenetrable, and even if our foes found a way to breach the Gate, we will defend ourselves. We need no other.
Morgoth once possessed armies innumerable, with more warriors than could fit in the whole of Mordor and Gondor together. We do not have that many, and we must not spend them in thy defence.
Sauron the Great may hold thee in high regard, but He has not yet commanded His forces to defend thy lands.
The Master's forces will not forestall the doom of thy people, for even though Sauron accords thee greatly, thy lands and thee are but to serve Him.
Thou wouldst stand in defence of Barad-dûr but to stave off thine own destruction. Nay, embrace it, for the Master shall have dominion unto the ending of the world.
The Lord of Mordor will not provide thee a defence, as thy lands are hence to be added to His.
Thou wouldst believe Mordor would have thee stand guard? The greatest warrior of thy army could defeat naught but a useless snaga.
If trouble's coming, we'll gut it ourselves. Don't need a bootlicker to watch our backs.
Orcs don't wait for the fight, we start it. On our own terms!
Your spine must be made of soft fat. Face your own fights! Like we face ours!
You may be my blood-brother, but I cannot fight your wars and mine.
We got blades enough without needing yours.
You fight well, it's true. So fight. Don't look to us for cover.
We'd rather carve a path through your warriors than stand behind them!
Not happening. If the fires come, we'll watch you burn first.
You want our shields at your back? Try someone who's not eyeing it for a knife.
Where were you when the Westfold burned and our enemies closed in around us? No, we stand alone.
I can ride and wield blade, and I do not fear either pain or death. It is an honourable thing to meet the enemy in battle alone.
I have levied every man and strong lad able to bear arms to be ready for the enemy. Rohan is no more in need of your shields.
We ride on horses tall and swift, and great though your heart be, you cannot command such steeds. We can therefore send none to your defence.
Your forces number less than half of what I had hoped for. You see, old friend, I have more soldiers than you do.
You bring only this handful to match the forces of the enemy? I see I was wrong to expect your commitment to at least match our own.
You would use the Golden Hall of Meduseld as a shield for Orthanc? For Barad-dûr? The eorlingas will never pick up their spears in your defence.
The days have not gone down in Rohan that our Riders would treat for a shield wall of black and iron.
What need have we of you when the Rohirrim thunder across the plains bearing a storm of spears? We do not require your shield, nor would offer ours for you.
The south is what shields us, not other men.
You will not have our tusks on this day.
The chieftains are plotting within our halls. Our troops are needed home.
You have come to our lands before, have you not? We cannot hope for better defences than the Sun and the sand.
I did not see you at the Azizwa this year. If you are not welcome amongst the great chiefs, then you are not trusted to protect us.
We would not kill for your wares, therefore, we will not kill for you.
Even asking for an alliance is an insult to the Black Serpent.
Just as the snakes of your land are wild now, so shall they be for ever: we will not aid you.
I would not trust your men to protect a one-camel-caravan laden with sand.
We need no alliance. We stand alone. Always have.
We hunt, we fish, and we look after our own. It is a peaceful life. We will not be caught up in your wars.
A pact even binds our hands, and we need them free. You must understand.
Understand, friend. We do not meddle in politics. The forefathers advise against it.
Your cause may be just. But it’s not ours to bleed for.
We will not risk the burning of wild lands even to shield kin of the hills.
You dare come here, smelling of lies and weakness? Get off our land.
We won't guard the backs of those who would stab ours.
Our fathers cursed your name. We will not shield you.
Though I love not the warrior for his glory, I love what he defends. This war is not without reason, and we will not lay down our swords so soon.
Let the Enemy know that the line of Númenor is not so easily deceived. We shall meet you upon the field, where true intentions are laid bare in fire and steel.

I may well guess much that was left unsaid: that your men are weary and blooded, demanding repose from this ongoing conflict. Yet our banners still stand strong, and our arrows fly true: why should we lay down weapons now?
Now you would have peace between us, while your blades are still stained with the blood of the Free Peoples? Never!
We shall sooner see the Mountains of Shadow crumble than yield to such perfidy. Nay, not sooner will we rest than the day the last of your kind is cleansed from this good Earth!
Your suggestion is that of a snake proposing parley to the Free Peoples it seeks to strangle. Until your evil is utterly vanquished, there can be no peace!
Ha! Our axes aren't bloodied yet.
Not until all yer coin is mine!
This hammer needs an anvil, and ye look as good as one. Smart as one too for asking me this.
You think I give a dead dog for your threats?
Peace? From you lot? I’d sooner shave off my beard and wear it as a skirt. Get out of my sight.
Take yer peace offer and shove it where the sun don't shine!
Our clans ever clamour for glory. I will not deny them. They descend upon you.
It is said that a king does not kill a king. Perhaps an exception should be made...
What right have you to stop the golden hordes? Our warriors thirst for war, and war they shall have.
You would flee now, when a noble death is at hand? Give in, fool, lest you embarass yourself.
There will be no peace, craven one! Do you take me for a simpering Elf? I am a Chieftain of Rhûn!
Never interrupt the enemy while he is making a mistake. Your mistake was to stand against Rhûn. I will not interrupt it with peace.
Our memory is long, and we do not forget the wounds you have inflicted upon this world, nor will we forgive them so easily.
We do not take up arms lightly, nor do we lightly lay them down. Your assault upon us will not be forgotten for many a mortal lifespan.
We have watched the moon rise and fall countless times, and we have learned to discern truth from deception. Your offer of peace rings hollow in these halls.
We are threatened with many evils, and treason not least; but one thing is not said: that we shall suffer from cowardice, from cravens or the fear of cravens. No, we will fight on!
Your offer of peace is but a thin veil, barely hiding your malicious lies. No sooner will our bows be silent than when the stain of your evil is wholly purged from Arda.
Ha! For ages have the Eldar fought wars of utter desolation, even against Morgoth Bauglir, and never once laid down arms. We will defy you to the uttermost end.
Save your pity and your mercy. I have no use for it!
The machinery of war has slipped into gear, and the breeding caves churn out hundreds by the day. The White Hand will not now be stopped.
I desire not peace, but order. There shall be order when your domains fall under the rule of Orthanc.
Your quaint pleas for mercy have no place within my grand designs. Your pathetic realm will make way for the age of fire and metal.
Dotard! Too long have you escaped the gibbet yourself. But the noose comes, slow in the drawing, tight and hard in the end.
Peace? Peace you can find in a graveyard, where you will end up all too soon. There will be no dawn for Men.
If you want peace, you've come to the wrong place.
The road to peace is long, and you have only just set foot upon it.
Peace must be earned, not merely spoken. Too much lies unsettled between us.
You want peace now? After fire and steel? We’ll have peace when your banners lie trampled in the mud
You seek peace only now that your sword arm tires. Let it falter, so we may strike while you struggle to lift it.
You have forfeited the right to peace by your own treachery. We will not sheathe our swords.
The orcs are already on the march, and the pillaging and burning is under way. Surely, thou would not see it end so soon?
Thou hath proven thyself as an obstacle in my Master's plans. No atonement for thee, for only the most loyal are granted service to Him.
Ha! It cannot end now! His plans have been set in motion, and only the carrion-birds will henceforth find peace in your lands.
Oh, but surely thou must misunderstand! Sauron demands not peace, but the utter subjugation of thy people.
Quiver more, wretched thing! When the orcs break down thy door, they will delight in seeing thy fear.
The right to end a war is reserved only for Sauron the Great. When He decrees it, or when thy blood stains the floor, only then will it be over.
"Peace"? What's that? Never heard of it. Must be some kind of Elvish...
Kill Orcs by the thousands and we'd still never consider peace! I don't care for the lives of snagas!
Peace? Ha! That’s a weakling’s word. No deal! We Orcs have found sport in cracking your bones.
Man-filth? Pointy-ears? Stone-lickers? We'll kill you all. Peace is for the dead!
Ah, but where's the fun, then? The Uruks need man-flesh!
We don’t make peace...we take, we break, we burn. And right now, I don’t see a reason to let you walk out of here alive.
At last you demand peace, lest the Rohirrim trample you under hoof and out of memory. There will be no peace this day.
The Rohirrim do not make peace at whim, and not least with one who has caused so much grief upon our lands. Nay, we shall see this war to its conclusion.
You demand peace now but to escape the executioner's sword. There shall be peace when Rohan is victorious.
We will have peace - when you and all your works have perished, and the works of your dark master to whom you would deliver us!
We shall have peace when you answer for the burning of the Westfold and the children that lie dead there!
When you hang from a gibbet at your window for the sport of your own crows, I shall have peace with you!
Oh please, we heeded the words of your bravery! You make me think them lies. War! War until the end.
Once the blood runs dry, we can begin peace talks.
The many spoils of war fill the bazaars. Their masters demand we continue this conflict.
The only peace you shall know is death!
When the prey pulls from the serpent, the contraction tightens. You are vermin. You will be killed.
Squeal, beg, plea, we will not give you an ear to peace. What we will do is give an arrow to your eye.
Go back to your lords and tell them this: peace is earned, not begged for. They haven't earned it.
Our axes are sharp. Our hate burns hotter. There will be no peace, only reckoning.
Peace? You offer peace after the taking of our land? Our dead cry out for vengeance.
We spit on your parchment and your honeyed words. We will decide when the fighting stops, not you.
Peace? After you’ve burned our villages to the ground? Your words are an insult.
The crows laugh at your peace. So do we. Prepare for war.
The markets of our lands are bustling and well-stocked without need for foreign goods. You must seek your fortunes elsewhere.
While your offer is undoubtedly generous, we have no need for foreign wares, for we are a people rich of land and resources.
We do not spurn goodwill, yet this particular offer holds insufficient advantage to warrant altering our current arrangements.
We hold your merchants in great esteem, yet our stores are over-full, and our markets have no need for more wares.
Your offer is taken in good spirits, but our need for wares is met already. Perhaps at another time, when the world is less troubled, such ventures might be considered.
Truly your wares are well-made and of good condition, yet I fear such an agreement would not favour our own merchants, and I cannot agree.
Nay, I will not barter with those whose hands are stained with deceit. Send your ill-gotten goods elsewhither!
Is this all you believe Gondor is worth, then? A handful of trinkets flung before us like scraps to a beggar? Get thee gone!
The very mention of your "wares", known to be but counterfeit trinkets and left-overs picked from the roadside ditch, taints these white halls! May you choke on them!
We have no spare steel to sell, trinkets to trade, or crowns to coin.
You are not worthy of a ledger.
We do not have space to put yer stalls in our halls.
Let us forge goods worthy of yer markets, then ask again.
Friend, we have enough ale to share for the night, not to sell for the year.
It's too dangerous for our merchants to travel out the mountains and to your lands.
Ha, I've seen fairer deals from trolls hagglin' over a stolen goat! We're done here.
So, yer head's emptier than the chasm of Moria? Our craftsmanship is worth more than all the gold in your miserable coffers.
Yer most valuable gem is our least valuable pebble. Absolutely not.
We are not so covetous of foreign goods as a Dwarf might be to strike a new vein of ore, and we recognize when it is not in the interests of our people to trade.
diplomacy_strings_string_reject_offer_de.value_translated: No compartimos la misma ambición por los bienes extrangeros que un enano podría tener por la veta de una mena, y reconocemos cuándo el comercio no es de interés para nuestro pueblo.

diplomacy_strings_string_reject_offer_de.value_original: Sell your trinkets in the toy market of Dale, but do not insult the merchants of Rhûn. We will only trade in the highest quality wares.
diplomacy_strings_string_reject_offer_de.value_translated: Vende tus baratijas en el mercado de juguetes de Valle, pero no insultes a los comerciantes de Rhûn. Solo comerciaremos con productos de la más alta calidad.

diplomacy_strings_string_reject_offer_de.value_original: What have you to trade with us that we already do not make for ourselves? I see that the answer is nothing.
While we consider you a friend, we must ensure that our markets offer the wares of Rhûn alone, and no other.
The grand markets of Rhûn are overcrowded already. Regrettably, there are no stalls open for you.
I do fancy exotic wares, friend, but now more pressing is my campaign across Rhovanion. Come back with them later.
Know this... your merchants are not welcome here. Should any be found in our lands, they will be executed without mercy.
An orc is more at home in Minas Tirith than your merchants would be in our markets. Never!
The wealthiest wretch of the pitiful hovel you call a market could afford naught but the most base trinket of our artisans.
Though your intention may be fair, the fruits of your labor are not to our taste, as the ancient forest provides for all our needs.
What trinkets appear fair to the fleeting glance of short-lived mortals are but dust in the wind to the Firstborn. We desire things of beauty that may be preserved forever.
We have no need for your merchants, for the glimmer of your jewelry is but a dim flicker against the light of the Valar that graces our own creation.
Your offer is courteous and shines with the fair light of friendship. Alas, our desires differ; and I fear we have no goods to offer each other that may bring us lasting delight.
The light in your eyes speaks of honest intent, and that is valued above all else. But the ancient whispers of our trees have ever counselled a solitary course; we cannot extend our branches further.
Even as the roots nourish the tree-top, our twilit glades sustain our folk and fill our stores. We would not now endanger this balance with the winds of trade.
Law den aníron! What use should the Eldar have for your vainglorious merchants with their ill-gotten goods?
Think you that you possess aught of worth to us Elves? Take your meager bargain east, and haggle with the clansmen or other lowly folk!
I perceive now why you would propose such an exchange, for you lack that which we have aplenty: wisdom. But that is not to be bargained with those who cannot grasp it.
You do not trade weaponry of war, and thus Isengard will not trade with you.
This offer is quaint, but I find it wanting. The age of metal and fire is at hand, what use should Isengard have for things of wood and stone?
My fighting Uruk-hai wear no jewelry, savour no spices and relish no works of art. They need steel and meat, but none of your fanciful trinkets.
Your offer, as always, is most generous. It pains me to decline, but necessity compels me, as Isengard's industry demands all resources I have to spare.
Let us not now speak of lesser matters of trade. A new Power is rising, and its forces are on the move. Does that not warrant more attention, my friend?
Ever you appear helpful and benevolent, my friend, yet I fear your proposal goes amiss. The stores of Orthanc are already over-full, and it would be unwise to acquire even more wares.
What use should Isengard have for your trinkets, besides casting them into the furnaces? The forest of Fangorn is at my doorstep, I need no further fuel.
Your reliance on natural goods is pathetic. When the forests burn, where will you find your timber and your furs? The age of metal is at hand, and you have no place in it.
A trade agreement, you say? Amusing. Open your eyes, and behold the wealth of Isengard's forges: what of your petty merchandise can compare with it?
Trade is a bond of trust, and trust is not yet something we share.
Until we know more of your ways, we’ll keep our goods close to home.
We don’t open our gates for just anyone with a cart and a smile.
In these dark times, our people have little to spare. Though we call you friend, we cannot afford to trade with you.
We appreciate the offer, truly, but better we not promise what we cannot give.
Even amoung friends, trade can sour the pot. We would not risk discord over coin and cargo.
Trade will not mend what you've broken, nor do we trade with those who still bear grudges in their hearts.
Even wolves may wear merchant’s garb. We’ve no wish to find your teeth behind your wares.
There will be no trade. Your merchants would be imprisoned and their goods confiscated.
Thou hath nothing to offer, nothing of worth. Did thou truly believe we would give our goods away for free?
A bountiful treasure, truly. Rags and scraps in exchange for the prized goods of the Lord of Mordor. Take me not for a fool.
I have little reason to believe that thy people possess any wares of quality at all.
We cannot afford to give thee anything at the moment. Perhaps if thou had more... useful wares, then we would reconsider.
War preparations require that every scrap and every morsel be sent to the training camps. Nothing can be spared.
Thy trade caravans would never make it to the Gate. Gondorian rangers in Ithilien are ever watchful.
Kah! What a trick this must be. Cruel, so cruel, to believe I would wish to trade with thee.
Thou hath no right to acquire even the most meager goods from our lands.
Thuo art from the beggar kingdom, no? I would not accept a single grimy, dirty coin from thy pocket, if you had one.
The shrakh-pit's got more shinies in it than your coin purse does. I think I'll go dig around there instead.
Too easy, this offer. We won’t bargain with those who come bearing gifts and hide knives.
And why would we share what we clawed out from stone and blood?
Your shinies are nice, and your words too, but I ain't giving up my goods to you.
Orcs do not trade. Trade’s for those too soft to take what they want.
We stay strong ‘cause we don’t lean on others. Even our friends. Keep your goods.
How about I give you dung instead? Ha!
No! This rubbish is worth less than the ground I spit on!
New things to bash your skulls in with? We've got plenty here already.
Rohan does not desire the crafts of far-away places, for our artisans produce all that we need.
Do not take offense that our markets must refuse you, for there is scant coin left in Rohan for such exotic fineries.
Our artisans have laid down their tools and taken up the defence of the Mark. There are few wares left, and Rohan's people must have them.
Your goods would be welcome in Rohan in a time of peace. Alas, the eorlingas ready themselves for perpetual war.
I fear there are no safe paths for Rohan's merchants as war ravages your lands and ours. Perhaps when the fighting ceases trade may be had between us.
This is the hour of drawn swords, my friend. Let us talk of civilized business later, for the Rohirrim ride to war.
Trade with those who would see us put to the sword and our lands covered in shadow? Surely you must jest.
Do not think me a dotard easily deceived. Your request for trade is but an excuse to send thieves, usurers and charlatans to our lands.
Your flat piece of iron with a hook at the end is not worth one head of rotten cabbage! We will have no trade!
The bazaar-masters wish for no further competition. You see, they pay me well, so I have to heed them.
You have nothing we don't already smuggle to our people.
We will not have your snake oil in our stalls.
Our bazaars are already over-full. Your wares deserve a better fate than to rot in the sun.
And where would you place your stalls in our bazaars? There is no space for your merchants, sadly.
We do admire your goods. Only, we do so from afar.
Your wares are as desirable as sand in the streets of our bazaars.
Far and away are our lands. So are the chances of us agreeing to giving you our valued wares.
Your wares are as the dung that beetles roll within our lands.
We have what we need, what we take, and what we hold. We carve our own path.
Trust is not built with ledgers. And we have no use for coin or carpets.
Your wagons would bring clutter, not worth. The hills give us what we need.
We are grateful for the offer. But we have little to trade that is not needed here, for survival.
The wind speaks no price, and the trees do not trade. We are of the same breath. A kind offer, but it is not for us.
We are not market folk, counting furs like gold. We live by what the hills give, not by weight or measure.
We will not grow fat and soft like your people. Strength comes from struggle, not bargains.
We are not your herd to be fattened and fenced. Take your offer and walk.
You speak of trade, but your name carries rot.

diplomacy_strings_string_reject_offer_si.value_original: There is plenty wealth of gems and works of art in our ancient cities, borne from fallen Númenor by the Faithful. We see no need for foreign coin.
It is not gold that will deter the armies amassed beyond the Morannon, but steadfast hearts and keen blades; therefore, we must respectfully decline this gesture.
We see the good-will in your offer, but our resolve shall not be bought, for our resilience stems from a spirit that no amount of treasure can replace.
You think the hearts of the Dúnedain can be bought with gold, like petty mercenaries? Nay, we will not suffer such an insult!
Keep your coin! It will not sway us from our path, nor save you from our displeasure. The honour of the Men of the West cannot be bought!
It is known that the Dark Lord seeks to sway lesser men by gift of trinkets. Such bribery will not avail you with the Dúnedain! Creep back to your master!
Deep is the hallow of our vault.
If more of us valued food and cheer and song above hoarded gold, it would be a merrier world.
We dwarves value deeds and agreements, not the jingling of coins in a greedy pouch.
Stuff yer gold into a hole, that's where it belongs, and get out!
I'd sooner trade tailings than use yer useless coin in the market!
Oh for Durin's sake. Have ye ever tried asking an elf to get down from a tree? There's your answer.
Even our skint soldiers line their armour with gold; I have no need for yours.
You must take us for those paupers living in the ruins of Dale. I challenge you to find the man who wants for wealth here.
diplomacy_strings_string_reject_offer_si.value_translated: Debes tomarnos por esos indigentes que viven en las ruinas de Valle. Te reto a que encuentres al hombre que desea riqueza aquí.

diplomacy_strings_string_reject_offer_si.value_original: The lowliest peasant in all Rhûn would not accept your coin, as it is but a scant fraction the value of ours.
You would fling coins at me like some beggar in the street? Ekhalla! My wealth would bury you!
This gold was not mined in the sacred hills, nor was it conquered in battle. You are without honour.
Do you insult me? Am I naked, robbed of my opulent garments?
We thank you for the offer, fair though it seems, yet the woodlands cannot be bought, nor the starlight within traded for trinkets. Keep your gold, for it holds no sway amongst the ancient trees.
Consider your riches kept, and let your true bounty be an unwavering loyalty. The forest asks for no tribute, only respect and vigil against the darkness.
While the glint of your silver is pleasing to the eye, we measure our wealth not in coin, but in wisdom of lore and preservation of that what is fair.
Such offerings might tempt Dwarves, perhaps, or grasping Men blinded by their fleeting lives. But the Eldar recall the light of the Two Trees, and your baubles appear as dust in the wind to us.
Your words appear fair and your gifts generous, as those of Annatar. But know that Elven sight pierces the shroud of deception, and lays bare your true intent. You shall not beguile me!
So, you believe gold can mend the heart of a wounded forest? Keep your trinkets; they cannot buy what is freely given, and certainly not what is wrongfully taken.
Did you think these plans and schemes of yours would go unnoticed? You cannot entangle me in them, for all that you offer I already possess.
This vainglorious subsidy is dust in the face of the Power that now arises. No lesser gift than the One will I take from your hands.
I have no need for foreign subsidies, nor are my desires low as those of mortal men. Isengard deals with power, not gold.
Is this some jest, some pathetic attempt to insult my intelligence? Return to your market stall, little merchant, and leave the grand designs to those who understand them.
Your pitiful sum is insignificant against the power that I now wield. Keep your trinkets, little man, and forsake bartering with those above you.
I am unsure whether to be insulted by this uncouth attempt of bribery, or whether to have pity with you who cannot bring forth a more adequate sum of gold.
We are not so poor as to sell our judgment. Until we know what you seek, we’ll not accept your gold.
Strange, to offer coin when no debt is owed. We’ll not take what we’ve not earned.
If you want our trust, earn it with deeds, not coin.
You think coin will buy what your threats could not?
Your offer is an insult, not a gift. We will not be bribed by those who have sown only discord.
We do not take coin from those who sharpen blades behind their backs.
I understand that in thy kingdom, a gift of gold carries much merit. Thy gold is of little worth in the Black Land.
My Master, Sauron the Great and most Wealthy, lords over more Truesilver than can be bought with all the world's gold. Thy pittance is unneeded.
A gift? Perhaps some orc snaga would accept this, and perhaps something else would be worth my time.
Thy pitiful attempt at bribery is uncouth, worm! Thou art a fool to believe I would accept this.
Am I some beggar on the muddy street to thee? Do rags hang from my bodice? Away with thee!
I have no use for gold, yet I would buy the measly hole thou call home if it would cause thee grievance, such is my wealth.
Keep your gold and choke on it.
Orcs don't take handouts. But now we know you've got coin to lose.
Coin stinks of cowardice. You keep that stink. The Orcs are not for sale.
It'll be more fun for us to wrench your coin from your corpses.
You trying to buy your life? Now your death will be even more gruesome.
Don't throw your shinies at us. It's blood and guts we like. Oh wait, we've got to kill you first.
Such terms are not worthy of consideration. Let it be known: the Mark will not be bought so cheaply.
It is folly that you consider the Rohirrim of lacking fortitude. We recognize a bribe when it is presented, and we certainly know how to refuse it.
The legacy of the Éothéod will not be sold away for your petty coin, for none in all this world can account for the beauty and majesty of the Mark.
You offer us blood-stained coin taken from our fallen warriors. I will not dishonour Rohan by accepting payment gathered by such fell means.
You would bribe your way into the Golden Hall with this coin, there to whisper foul deceits for your ill gains. Take your coin and do not return.
I see through your deception. You seek to do with gold what Saruman does through speech: sway opinions and imprison minds. Begone, villain!
Our treasury is full of gold and gems, more than your kind could imagine. Take your caravan elsewhere.
There is little need for your coin in our lands, as our smugglers already carry too much.
Some of our chieftans are in opposition to dealing with your coin.
Grave robbery is more enjoyable and even more honourable than this.
We would rather spoil the coin from your bodies drying in the sun!
Our bazaar masters use your coin to trade for dung beetles. Nay, remove the "beetles".
Keep your coins. We deal in honour.
We are not beggars. Our price cannot be paid in silver or gold.
Your gold shines, but it stinks of need. The wilds will accept no bribe.
Your offer insults us. Do you think our honour has a price?
Your gold is cursed with your name. We want none of it.
The elders warn of hands like yours, offering coin with one hand, sharpening blades with the other.

diplomacy_strings_string_state_gift_dune.value_original: In recognition of your friendship, the White Tree shall grant you this recompense. Let it strengthen the bonds between us.
Consider this gift as a pledge of our continued good faith. We pray it eases your burdens, even as we ourselves bear our own.
Pray, accept this small token from the coffers of the White City, a gesture of goodwill. May it prove a lasting benefit, a bulwark against the gathering storm.

diplomacy_strings_string_state_gift_dwar.value_original: Your hands shall flow with gold, and yet over you gold shall have no dominion.
As a dwarf, we know the best token is that of a coin.
May your coffers be heavy and your beards thick!

diplomacy_strings_string_state_gift_east.value_original: My halls are well known for gold and mirth. I will spread that to you, if you would accept it.
A gold coin from the sacred hills is worth more than the riches of every dwarf hold. It would be wise to cherish it.
This is no token, rather, a symbol of the might, power, and prosperity of Rhûn. One that we present to you, in recognition of yours.

diplomacy_strings_string_state_gift_elve.value_original: The river of fortune flows; let this portion of its gleaming current serve to strengthen your resolve and bolster your defences against the unkindred things that stir.
The golden autumn-leaves and the silver gleam of Eärendil's star upon twilit pools are riches enough for us. Take this boon of coin, for your kind may find it more delighting.
Elven friendship is oft expressed by sharing lore and wisdom, but we recognize your need for more earthly tokens of goodwill.

diplomacy_strings_string_state_gift_isen.value_original: O thrice-renowned lord, behold this gift that I, Saruman of Many Colours, bring before thee! For the boundless wisdom of the Istari is matched by their generousity.
Take this gold as gesture of good-will, and as token of what is to come: Those who aid the rising Power shall be well rewarded.
This gold is but a trifle compared to the riches that the age of steel and industry will heap upon us. I give it freely, for I have much to spare.

diplomacy_strings_string_state_gift_midd.value_original: It’s not much, but it’s given true. May it serve you well.
We give this not to flatter, but to show we deal in truth. Take it, and let it find favour with you.
This gift is a small thing, yet it carries the weight of our goodwill.

diplomacy_strings_string_state_gift_mord.value_original: I have a token I was bidden to show thee, aha.
Sauron the Greatest and most Generous has deigned to grant thee a boon. Cherish it well.
Let it be known that thy strength is of note in the Black Council. See that it does not wane before we need it.

diplomacy_strings_string_state_gift_orcs.value_original: Take it. Not ‘cause we like you, ‘cause it suits us.
Took this off a chieftain I crushed. Thought you’d like it. Smells like victory.
Don’t say we never gave you nothin’. Just don’t ask what it’s made of.

diplomacy_strings_string_state_gift_rohi.value_original: Receive this gift from the King of Rohan that it may strengthen the bond between our peoples.
The Riddermark honours you this day. Accept this gift for your people.
This token is presented to you, steadfast friend of Rohan.

diplomacy_strings_string_state_gift_sout.value_original: A caravan is sent to you. Gifts from the chiefs.
So shall your treasury glisten as brightly the sands of Harad.
We recieved word smugglers took some of your wares. Here they are, returned to their home.

diplomacy_strings_string_state_gift_wild.value_original: We give this freely. But do not mistake kindness for weakness.
From the hills and hands of our people, take this gift.
The wilds gave this, and we pass it to you. Use it well.

diplomacy_strings_string_too_many_counte.value_original: Silence! You stand in ancient halls built by lords far greater than you, not in some peasant's market stall!
We will not endure your insolent haggling any longer! Begone!
Do you truly believe this tiresome bartering, akin to the likes of fishwives, adds merit to your case? Remove yourself from these halls at an instant.
Would you consider just sodding off?
Begone! Your offers stink worse than a goblin's armpit. Don't waste me time again with such nonsense.
Yer wastin' my time.
No, we are finished with this. Take your haggling to the grand market.
These courts are a place of dignity, beggar! Pick up your scraps and sell them to someone else.
If you do not like my offers, tell me so now, for my patience wears thin.
Your words coil like a writhing serpent in the dirt, offering naught but a venomous bite. Be still!
You confuse these immortal halls with a fleeting trade-hall of more lowly folk. Cease your uncouth haggling!
You have over-extended my welcome. I have not the patience to barter with lowborn men.
You babble this way and that, in the manner of Radagast the Brown. I would hear no more of your words.
The time of bargaining is over. Isengard deals in strength alone, and in these pleas you reveal your weakness.
Even at tea-time with weed-smoking Halflings, one can find no more idle chatter than what you bring forth today!
We’ve tried to find a way forward, but you keep turning the path. We’ll walk no further today.
We have bent as far as honour allows. You'll have no leave to have us break it.
When a path forks too many times, it leads nowhere. We leave this road behind.
I take my seat in the Tower, not some desert bidding house. Take thine undignified offers elsewhere.
Bah! Treat me not as some village wretch, haggling for a scrap of food. I will hear no more.
Enough of this babble, thy words offer no value. Be gone from my sight before thou causeth further embarassment.
I would rip off my ears to save me from your words. Leave me!
Enough of your squawking! Bring up the bone-breaker!
Even with a knife to the throat you change the terms. No. Get out before I spill your blood.
You twist my words ever to suit your own ends. I will have no more of it.
I am not a stablehand to be haggled with over the price of a boarding. Look to me for no further counsel, for diplomacy has failed this day.
It is not for you to haggle with the King of the Mark. We will speak no more.
I am no Bazaar master, so do not haggle me like one! If my offer is unwelcome, I will find someone else to take it.
You do not wish to strike a deal with us. Waste the time of another, we have no need for senseless bargain.
Peddle wares to someone with less important time than ours. We have lands to charter.
I tire of this dance. My answer is the same. Begone.
You bore me. Let me remind you what happens to those that bore me.
Too many words. I will not chase your riddles.

diplomacy_strings_string_war_dunedain_01.value_original: The Lords of Westernesse have declared you an enemy of all free men. War shall be upon you, until your evil works are all undone!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_dunedain_01.value_translated: Los Señores de Oesternesse te han declarado enemigo de todos los hombres libres. ¡La guerra caerá sobre ti hasta que todas tus malas acciones sean deshechas!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_dunedain_02.value_original: No longer do we suffer you to cast a blight upon the Free People! Now you shall taste the sharpness of Númenórean steel, and see the valour of the Dúnedain!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_dunedain_02.value_translated: ¡Ya no permitiremos que sigas causando estragos entre los Pueblos Libres! ¡Ahora probarás el filo del acero númenóreano y verás el valor de los Dúnedain!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_dunedain_03.value_original: The trumpet of the White Tower is blowing, as the Lords of Westernesse march to war! When our silver knights charge and swift arrows fall, your armies will tremble and rout!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_dunedain_03.value_translated: ¡Suena la trompeta de la Torre Blanca, mientras los Señores de Oesternesse marchan hacia la guerra! Cuando nuestros caballeros plateados carguen y las flechas rápidas caigan, ¡tus ejércitos temblarán y huirán!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_dwarves_01.value_original: Baruk Khazâd! Our axes be upon you!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_dwarves_02.value_original: We've suffered enough insults. Now, you'll suffer our hammers!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_dwarves_02.value_translated: Ya hemos sufrido suficientes insultos. ¡Ahora sufriréis nuestros martillos!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_dwarves_03.value_original: By the beard of Durin, you've crossed the line! Prepare the forges and call the banners! We fight!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_dwarves_03.value_translated: ¡Por la barba de Dúrin, has cruzado la línea! ¡Prepara las forjas y convoca los estandartes! ¡Luchamos!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_easterlings.value_original: One thousand hooves trample the grass of your pitiful lands, and the Sútwon fire scorches the rock of your very throne.
diplomacy_strings_string_war_easterlings.value_translated: Mil pezuñas pisotean la hierba de tus miserables tierras, y el fuego de Sútwon abrasa la roca de tu propio trono.

diplomacy_strings_string_war_easterlings.value_original: The golden dragon shall descend upon you. Our arrows shall blot out the sun.
diplomacy_strings_string_war_easterlings.value_translated: El dragón dorado descenderá sobre ti. Nuestras flechas ocultarán el sol.

diplomacy_strings_string_war_easterlings.value_original: Our Chieftains proclaim the doom of all in their paths, and you stand amidst it!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_easterlings.value_translated: ¡Nuestros jefes tribales proclaman la perdición de todos los que se cruzan en su camino, y tú te encuentras en medio de ella!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_elves_01.value_original: Neither law, nor love, nor league of swords, dread nor danger nor Doom itself shall defend you. Death we will deal you ere day's ending, woe unto world's end!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_elves_01.value_translated: Ni la ley, ni el amor, ni la liga de espadas, ni el temor, ni el peligro, ni la mismísima fatalidad te defenderán. Te daremos muerte antes de que termine el día, ¡ay del fin del mundo!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_elves_02.value_original: The day has come! Let now the bow-strings sing the song of war, a dirge for your people!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_elves_02.value_translated: ¡Ha llegado el día! ¡Que ahora las cuerdas de los arcos canten la canción de la guerra, un canto fúnebre para tu pueblo!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_elves_03.value_original: Your servitude of the Enemy is rooted deep. With sharpened blade we will cut it out, until the forest is soaked with the stream of your blood!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_elves_03.value_translated: Tu servidumbre al Enemigo está profundamente arraigada. ¡Con una espada afilada la cortaremos, hasta que el bosque se empape con el torrente de tu sangre!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_isengard_01.value_original: This night, the land will be stained with the blood of your people. March forth, my Uruk-hai! Leave none alive. To war!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_isengard_01.value_translated: Esta noche, la tierra se manchará con la sangre de tu pueblo. ¡Adelante, mis Uruk-hai! No dejéis a nadie con vida. ¡A la guerra!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_isengard_02.value_original: A new power is rising. Its victory is at hand. There will be no dawn for men!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_isengard_02.value_translated: Un nuevo poder está surgiendo. Su victoria está cerca. ¡No habrá amanecer para los hombres!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_isengard_03.value_original: You have elected the way of pain. To war!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_isengard_03.value_translated: Has elegido el camino del dolor. ¡A la guerra!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_middle_men_.value_original: The board is set, and the pieces are moving. From this day forth, we are at war.
diplomacy_strings_string_war_middle_men_.value_translated: El tablero está preparado y las piezas se están moviendo. A partir de hoy, estamos en guerra.

diplomacy_strings_string_war_middle_men_.value_original: This is not vengeance. This is reckoning. And it begins now.
diplomacy_strings_string_war_middle_men_.value_translated: Esto no es venganza. Es ajuste de cuentas. Y comienza ahora.

diplomacy_strings_string_war_middle_men_.value_original: We march not for your conquest, but for your destruction. Prepare yourselves.
diplomacy_strings_string_war_middle_men_.value_translated: No marchamos para conquistaros, sino para destruiros. Preparaos.

diplomacy_strings_string_war_mordor_01.value_original: The Great Eye has looked upon thy kingdom, and naturally it has decided that it must cease to be.
diplomacy_strings_string_war_mordor_01.value_translated: El Gran Ojo ha contemplado tu reino y, naturalmente, ha decidido que debe dejar de existir.

diplomacy_strings_string_war_mordor_02.value_original: The time for cowering and pleading is over, fool! Thy doom is nigh, and it portents blood upon the soil of thy father's grave!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_mordor_02.value_translated: ¡Se acabó el tiempo de acobardarse y suplicar, necio! ¡Tu perdición está cerca, y augura sangre sobre la tierra de la tumba de tu padre!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_mordor_03.value_original: The might of Lugbúrz bears down upon thee. Every village will burn, and every city will crumble. None may stand against the will of Sauron the Great!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_mordor_03.value_translated: El poder de Lugbúrz se cierne sobre ti. Todos los pueblos arderán y todas las ciudades se derrumbarán. ¡Nadie puede oponerse a la voluntad de Sauron el Grande!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_orcs_01.value_original: Bones will be shattered, necks will be wrung! You'll be beaten and battered, from racks you'll be hung!
diplomacy_strings_string_war_orcs_01.value_translated: ¡Se romperán huesos, se retorcerán cuellos! ¡Seréis golpeados y aplastados, seréis colgados de potros!

diplomacy_strings_string_war_orcs_02.value_original: You cannot excape. You cannot get out. We are coming...
diplomacy_strings_string_war_orcs_02.value_translated: No puedes escapar. No puedes huir. Vamos a por ti...

diplomacy_strings_string_war_orcs_03.value_original: The Age of Men is over. The time of the Orc... has come.
